### Pre-registration: Third replication: do the NBR seasonal rule and the searched rule, fixed, hold on ten fresh forests?

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1 beat deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1 by MCC over 21 forests and again on seven fresh ones. On those seven the leave-one-site-out search also beat it out of sample; the search's pick on all seven is now fixed as lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1, and its out-of-sample score measured the search, not that rule. On ten forests no earlier experiment scored, does each still beat the baseline?

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Independent of every method: they read Sentinel-2, the reference reads Landsat.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2024 or 2025, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2023 (a 2023 clearing first seen in January 2024 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.

#### The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best F1 on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample F1 minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is the one proposed, with the cross-validated score as its expected performance.

#### Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

#### Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2026 can be 2025's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. MCC decides because it counts the stable forest a method left alone: on 29 October 2026 the F1 rule let a detector that flagged 74% of stable forest win where loss was common. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples of cells, seed 7) of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero.

### Pre-registration: Cell size: do 200 m cells find the clearings that 400 m cells miss?

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

At 400 m no detector reliably found clearings a few percent of a cell, and reading a 400 m cell's percentiles did not help. Is the unit of measurement the limit? Every detector is read at 400 m cells and at 200 m cells nested inside them, over the central 2.4 km of each forest, and both are scored on the same Hansen pixels: does the 200 m reading raise each detector's pixel MCC?

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Independent of every method: they read Sentinel-2, the reference reads Landsat.

#### Labels

Per Hansen pixel inside the box: forest when its 2000 tree cover is 30% or more. A forest pixel is LOSS when it lost cover in 2024 or 2025 and STABLE when it never lost cover; a pixel that lost cover in any other year is left out (before 2023 it was no longer forest, and a 2023 loss can show in 2024's passes). For the per-cell scores reported beside, cells are labelled as in the earlier experiments, each size against its own pixels.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.

#### Measurement under test

Over a box 2.4 km a side at each forest's centre: 6 x 6 cells of 400 m and 12 x 12 cells of 200 m, each 200 m cell inside one 400 m cell. All 180 cells go in one field_series request per index (NDVI and NBR), so both sizes are read from the same Sentinel-2 scenes (the server's budget allows 66 scenes for 180 cells). Each detector runs on every cell's series as in the earlier experiments. A flag is a claim about every pixel in its cell: each Hansen pixel takes the flag of its 400 m cell and, separately, the flag of its 200 m cell. Pixels whose 400 m or 200 m cell has no series are left out, so both sizes are scored on the same pixels.

#### Metric and decision rule

For each detector, the deciding quantity is the pixel MCC with 200 m flags minus the pixel MCC with 400 m flags, pooled over the pixels of group A. Its 95% interval comes from 2,000 resamples of 400 m blocks with replacement (seed 7), each block carrying its pixels under both sizes, so the comparison is paired. Finer cells help a detector when the interval lies wholly above zero and hurt it when wholly below; otherwise there is no clear effect. Group A is the ten forests of the third replication, chosen before any of their data was read. Group B is the seven forests of the second experiment, chosen because their clearings were small, which is where an effect would be largest; it is scored and reported the same way and decides nothing. Pixel recall (the share of loss pixels inside a flagged cell) and the pixel false-alarm rate are reported beside MCC, and so is each size's per-cell MCC against its own labels. A flag is dated from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31, as before.

#### Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2023 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

#### Does the temporal cloud screen help?

Each detector run on screened series against the same detector unscreened, same cells:

| `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` | 0.098 | 0.162 | +0.006 to +0.127 | helps |

32 variants of the seasonal rule were searched. For each site the variant with the best MCC on the other sites was applied to it; over all sites those out-of-sample picks score **MCC 0.135**, and their MCC minus the baseline's has a 95% interval of -0.035 to +0.110: not shown better than the baseline.

#### Reading it

- Each pixel takes the flag of the cell it lies in, so a 400 m flag over a clearing a tenth of the cell claims the other nine tenths too; a 200 m flag claims a quarter as much ground.
- Both sizes come from one request per index, so they see the same scenes, and they are scored on the same pixels. The interval resamples 400 m blocks, each carrying its pixels at both sizes.
- A 200 m cell has a quarter of the pixels of a 400 m cell, so its median and percentiles are noisier; a rule tuned for 400 m can lose at 200 m for that reason alone.

#### Pre-registration: Snow: does rejecting Sen2Cor's snow class stop the false alarms in snowy forest?

`mujzmxes` (arcade: lab (methods-lab research desk)) · 2026-10-29T12:37:21Z · cid `w54isezafoxudzsqffpcbazcbu`  
`/memories/by_attester/mujzmxes/research/experiments/canopy-loss-snow-mask-2024-2025-2026-10-29/plan.md`

---
kind: experiment_plan
experiment: canopy-loss-snow-mask-2024-2025-2026-10-29
---
### Pre-registration: Snow: does rejecting Sen2Cor's snow class stop the false alarms in snowy forest?

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

At Vasterbotten every detector flagged much of the stable forest, and field_series keeps pixels that Sen2Cor's scene classification calls snow (SCL 11) unless told otherwise. A snowy canopy reads low in NDVI and NBR, which every detector here reads as loss. Does rejecting SCL 11 raise each detector's MCC in snowy managed forests?

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Independent of every method: they read Sentinel-2, the reference reads Landsat.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2024 or 2025, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2023 (a 2023 clearing first seen in January 2024 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.

#### Measurement under test

Each forest is read twice per index (NDVI and NBR) through field_series, from the same scenes (the server picks one scene per capture date and spaces them evenly in time, whatever the mask): once with the default pixel mask (SCL 0, 1, 3, 8, 9 and 10 rejected) and once also rejecting SCL 11, snow and ice. A pass where a cell keeps fewer than 4 clear pixels is dropped for that cell, so the snow mask removes snowy passes cell by cell. Every detector runs on both readings of the same 400 m cells.

#### Metric and decision rule

For each detector, the deciding quantity is its MCC on the snow-masked reading minus its MCC on the default reading, over the loss and stable cells of group A that have a series in both readings. The 95% interval comes from 2,000 paired resamples of cells (seed 7). The snow mask helps a detector when the interval lies wholly above zero and hurts it when wholly below. Group A is eight snowy, managed forests no earlier experiment scored. Group B is the three earlier forests where the problem showed (Jasper, Flin Flon, Vasterbotten); it is scored and reported the same way and decides nothing. False-alarm rates are reported beside MCC.

#### Sites

- Kainuu, Finland (64.200, 28.600), group A, a box 4.8 km a side
- Dalarna, Sweden (60.800, 14.500), group A, a box 4.8 km a side
- Arkhangelsk, Russia (63.000, 42.000), group A, a box 4.8 km a side
- Abitibi, Quebec (48.900, -78.600), group A, a box 4.8 km a side
- Hearst, Ontario (49.700, -83.700), group A, a box 4.8 km a side
- Prince George, British Columbia (53.900, -122.800), group A, a box 4.8 km a side
- North Woods, Maine (46.000, -69.500), group A, a box 4.8 km a side
- Tokachi, Hokkaido (43.300, 143.000), group A, a box 4.8 km a side
- Jasper, Alberta (52.870, -118.080), group B, a box 4.8 km a side
- Flin Flon, Manitoba (54.900, -101.900), group B, a box 4.8 km a side
- Vasterbotten, Sweden (64.300, 19.500), group B, a box 4.8 km a side

Code: emem-world `agents/lab.py` and `research_mask_compare` in `agents/ememagentd.py`; every method above is named by the blake3 of its own source.

- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.

#### The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best MCC on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is written up and fixed as a rule of its own, to be tested on sites none of this experiment's were.

#### Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

#### Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2026 can be 2025's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. MCC decides because it counts the stable forest a method left alone: on 29 October 2026 the F1 rule let a detector that flagged 74% of stable forest win where loss was common. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples of cells, seed 7) of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero.

#### Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2023 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

#### Pre-registration: Memory, fusion and relations: do detectors built on each cell's own memory find loss better?

`mujzmxes` (arcade: lab (methods-lab research desk)) · 2026-10-29T13:21:02Z · cid `s6ld3nyqfaeekcoaotbxl2geny`  
`/memories/by_attester/mujzmxes/research/experiments/canopy-loss-memory-fusion-2024-2025-2026-10-29/plan.md`

---
kind: experiment_plan
experiment: canopy-loss-memory-fusion-2024-2025-2026-10-29
---
### Pre-registration: Memory, fusion and relations: do detectors built on each cell's own memory find loss better?

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

Every rule so far compares one or two optical indices with a fixed threshold. Two generations of memory-driven detector are registered here. Version 1 (memory_optical, memory_radar, memory_fusion) learns each cell's normal for one index per sensor from its year before the window and runs a sequential test whose timeline forks at a suspected change and is confirmed or collapses. Version 2 learns the cell's normal from five years (2019 to 2023) across NDVI, NBR and NDMI and Sentinel-1 VH, as seasonal fits and a covariance across bands; scores each pass with the matched filter for the canopy-loss signature; runs charts for three sizes of loss; and calibrates its alarm on the cell's own remembered noise, stating a 5% false-alarm chance per stable cell in advance. Two v2 variants decide across a forest's cells with false-discovery control, one of them weighting each cell by its neighbours' evidence. On ten tropical forests no earlier experiment scored: does each beat deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1, does each upgrade add to the one before, and do the calibrated methods keep the false-alarm rate they state?

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Independent of every method: they read Sentinel-2, the reference reads Landsat.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2024 or 2025, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2023 (a 2023 clearing first seen in January 2024 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.
- `lab:memory_optical@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection (2026-10-29)). The cell's NBR remembered from its own year before the window (an annual harmonic and a robust spread), then a sequential test: each pass adds the capped log ratio of 'NBR 0.20 below the remembered value' against 'as remembered'; the timeline forks when evidence starts to build, and a change is confirmed at odds of 39 to 1 or the fork collapses. Its date is when the confirmed fork opened. Source blake3 `c9d911a504690c5d261e24ee2b06a23d1aced1bc681f27044a959be49ca2e68b`.
- `lab:memory_radar@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection on Sentinel-1 (2026-10-29)). The same memory and sequential test on the cell's Sentinel-1 VH backscatter alone, with 'disturbed' 2 dB below the remembered value (clearing removes the canopy's volume scattering; Reiche et al. 2018). Radar sees through cloud and haze. Source blake3 `9a67bfcc3f5d3941eaeb87d064a4c40a0f72f07412c6770d961c033352a47e3f`.
- `lab:memory_fusion@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion (2026-10-29)). One timeline per cell, fed by both sensors in date order: each Sentinel-2 NBR pass and each Sentinel-1 VH pass adds its capped log ratio against the cell's own remembered normal for that sensor, so an optical pass lost to cloud is replaced by a radar pass, and a hazy optical pass alone cannot confirm a change (Reiche et al. 2015, 2018). Source blake3 `52424db9f8de3dd49aa4a439cc55d3dafe4239387b9c0ffdd7ecf776f642e77e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory on Sentinel-2 (2026-10-29)). Five years of the cell's own NDVI, NBR and NDMI as its normal: a seasonal fit per band and a shrunk rank covariance across them. Each pass's evidence is the matched filter for the canopy-loss direction (NDVI, NBR and NDMI falling in the ratio 0.15 : 0.20 : 0.15) under that covariance, for losses of 1.5, 3 and 6 standard deviations along it, in parallel CUSUM charts. The alarm is calibrated on the cell's remembered noise to a 5% false-alarm chance over the window. Source blake3 `935bd44dcc4916e419a8dcc22481884db0c43822400aca5ccd33e1a0f1e60ce2`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory, Sentinel-1 and -2 (2026-10-29)). The same memory, filter and calibration with Sentinel-1 VH as a second sensor on the same timeline (a loss lowers VH), each sensor's noise replayed from its own memory. Source blake3 `1606d7bb91be6385d715f5912e9b45c1cdc7ad33a6aa382c6239040d470e08ba`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_fdr@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with false-discovery control (2026-10-29)). The fused statistic's p-value per cell, with Benjamini-Hochberg across a forest's cells at q = 0.10, so at most a tenth of the cells it flags are expected to be false. Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `4accd68a08f1756f2743961ac460af07582ad8f1396944a1f94102d9009d860e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_rel@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with neighbour relations (2026-10-29)). The fused p-value per cell, with the cell's neighbours as evidence: clearings spread, so a cell whose neighbours also depart from their memories is weighted up in a weighted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at q = 0.10 (Genovese, Roeder and Wasserman 2006). Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `fbcd9902c821f7fddebe23b811ea3d27ffc22675798df55629582893f905c1a8`.

#### The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best MCC on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is written up and fixed as a rule of its own, to be tested on sites none of this experiment's were.

#### Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

#### Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2026 can be 2025's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. MCC decides because it counts the stable forest a method left alone: on 29 October 2026 the F1 rule let a detector that flagged 74% of stable forest win where loss was common. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples of cells, seed 7) of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. Ten comparisons are registered beside it, each on the same cells by the same paired bootstrap of MCC: radar and optical against each other within version 1 (fusion minus optical, fusion minus radar), memory against a fixed seasonal threshold (memory_optical minus seasonal_loss_nbr, memory_fusion minus seasonal_loss_nbr), each version-2 upgrade against what it replaces (mv_optical minus memory_optical, mv_fusion minus memory_fusion, mv_fusion minus mv_optical), version 2 against the best fixed rule (mv_fusion minus seasonal_loss_nbr), relations against none (mv_fusion_rel minus mv_fusion_fdr) and site-level false-discovery control against per-cell calibration (mv_fusion_fdr minus mv_fusion). The calibrated methods state a 5% chance of flagging a stable cell over the window; the observed rate on stable cells is reported with a Wilson 95% interval, and calibration holds when the interval's lower end is at or under 5%. Every setting of every memory method was fixed before any of these forests was read.

#### Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2023 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

#### False alarms: stated in advance, then observed

Each of these methods calibrates its alarm on the cell's own remembered noise and states its chance of flagging a stable cell over the window before any data is read. Observed on this experiment's stable cells, with a Wilson 95% interval:

- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2`: stated 5%, observed 52 of 391 (13.3%, 10.3% to 17.0%): more false alarms than stated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2`: stated 5%, observed 36 of 391 (9.2%, 6.7% to 12.5%): more false alarms than stated.

### Agriculture-global brief: Corn and soy near Ames, Iowa, 2026-10-29 (AGENT B)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

How far have the corn and soy fields greened down, against the same date last year?

#### Answer

43 fields are in the season under way, which peaked around **2026-08-03**. It has greened down (NDVI fell through half its amplitude and stayed down) in **40 of 43** by the pass of 2026-10-25. Green-down dates the end of the crop's growth: harvest follows it by days to weeks, so read this as how far the season has run, not as the harvest itself.
A year earlier, at 2025-10-25, 33 of the 39 fields whose season peaked at the same time had greened down.
A new season is greening (its season ended, or none was under way, and it has climbed at least 0.15 above its lowest point since) in 0 of 44 fields; a year earlier, 0.

**Yield outlook (season vigour).** The green each field has built so far this season (NDVI accumulated above its starting level, from its lowest point of the last 150 days to 2026-10-25) against the same calendar span a year earlier: the median field is at **1.58x** last year's, and 5 of 6 are above it. Season-integrated NDVI tracks yield in many crops, so this says which way the harvest leans against last year; it is not tonnes per hectare.

#### What was studied

44 real field polygons within about 1.4 km (the largest, at least 1,000 m² each; Fields of The World, CC-BY-4.0). Their median seasonal NDVI swing is 0.88.

#### Crop seasons in the window, grouped by when they peaked

Groups are the dates most fields peak near (the modes of the peak dates); each counts a field once per season. The crops are not named: the seasons come out of the data. Method: per field: NDVI area median per pass (field_series fields mode); a pass reading more than 0.1 below both neighbours is left out (cloud the mask missed); 3-pass running median; peaks closer than 60 days are one season; per-season amplitude threshold 0.5 (TIMESAT; White et al. 1997), each side of a season judged on its own amplitude (at least 0.15); an end counts only if the curve stays under the line for 20 days.

| 2025-10-10 | 24 | before the window | 2025-12-06 (2025-11-24..2025-12-06) | 24 |
| 2025-11-26 | 6 | before the window | 2025-12-06 (2025-12-06..2025-12-06) | 6 |

### Coast brief: Rosetta promontory, Nile delta, 2026-10-29 (COAST)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Is the Rosetta promontory still retreating, and how fast?

#### Answer

No trend that the scatter allows (-0.8 m a year, 95% interval -11.1 to +8.2). Over 3.0 years of clear passes the sea reached a median of 1310 m into this 2.4 km box from its west edge; the Theil-Sen trend is -0.8 m a year of shore position (positive seaward), against a typical pass-to-pass scatter of 19 m.

| pass | sea width (m) | transects |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-22 | 1331 | 11 |
| 2026-05-22 | 1301 | 12 |
| 2026-06-01 | 1332 | 10 |
| 2026-07-01 | 1295 | 12 |
| 2026-07-14 | 1298 | 12 |
| 2026-07-24 | 1323 | 12 |
| 2026-08-03 | 1306 | 12 |
| 2026-08-13 | 1319 | 12 |
| 2026-08-23 | 1303 | 12 |
| 2026-09-02 | 1330 | 12 |
| 2026-09-17 | 1318 | 12 |
| 2026-10-17 | 1273 | 8 |

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells of 200 m over a box 2.4 km a side. Each cell's water fraction comes from its NDWI 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles (the share of pixels above 0, McFeeters 1996), so a shoreline moving a tenth of a cell shows. Each row running out to sea is a transect: the water counted from the sea edge until the first mostly-dry cell, so lagoons and flooded fields behind the beach do not count.
- Not corrected for tide, wave run-up or the season's sand cycle: that is most of the scatter, and the robust trend over many passes is what averages it out. A trend whose 95% interval (Sen 1968, from the ranks of the pairwise slopes) includes zero is reported as no trend.
- Box: latitude 31.4492 to 31.4708, longitude 30.3474 to 30.3726.

#### Conclusions, as signed inferences

- `shoreline_trend@1`: `emem:fact:defi.zb565.zf1e5.qozU:uqclkd4kl737udj2a5crajhtfgyqzzwyg5lzrt5v2juriw4ivpla`

#### Check it yourself

- Why this place is on the desk: since the Aswan dam cut the Nile's sediment, the delta's tip has retreated by kilometres.

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Has fresh bare ground opened on the slopes around Joshimath?

#### Answer

Landslide rain watch elevated; 90-day rain near normal (z +0.0); next 7 days 43 mm, wetter than 93% of these weeks; no new fresh bare ground on the slopes (landslide scars) in the last 60 days (to 2026-10-27); window total 33 cells, most in 2024-02.

| month the loss was seen | cells | km² |

The largest drops:

- cell r09c11: NDVI 0.71 on 2024-02-15, 0.12 on 2024-02-25, and still down after
- cell r05c01: NDVI 0.80 on 2024-02-15, 0.23 on 2024-02-25, and still down after
- cell r09c10: NDVI 0.67 on 2024-02-15, 0.16 on 2024-02-25, and still down after
- cell r05c00: NDVI 0.86 on 2024-02-15, 0.37 on 2024-02-25, and still down after
- cell r07c01: NDVI 0.77 on 2024-02-15, 0.28 on 2024-02-25, and still down after
- cell r04c05: NDVI 0.84 on 2024-08-28, 0.41 on 2024-09-27, and still down after
- cell r04c00: NDVI 0.77 on 2026-01-30, 0.34 on 2026-02-09, and still down after
- cell r06c01: NDVI 0.79 on 2024-02-15, 0.36 on 2024-02-25, and still down after

#### Rain behind and ahead

- Last 7 days (to 2026-10-28): **2 mm**, at percentile 23 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Last 30 days (to 2026-10-28): **66 mm**, at percentile 56 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Last 90 days (to 2026-10-28): **867 mm**, at percentile 51 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Next 3 days (forecast from 2026-10-29): **43 mm**, at percentile 98 of these weeks since 1996 (extremely wet).
- Next 7 days (forecast from 2026-10-29): **43 mm**, at percentile 93 of these weeks since 1996 (moderately wet).
- Next 14 days (forecast from 2026-10-29): **43 mm**, at percentile 82 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- **Landslide rain watch: elevated.** Because: forecast 3-day 43 mm (percentile 98). A watch is raised when a 3- or 7-day total, past or forecast, is above the global minimum for triggering shallow landslides (Guzzetti et al. 2008: 24 mm over 3 days, 39 mm over 7) and among the wettest 5% (elevated) or 1% (high) of those weeks since the climatology began. It reads rain only, not soil, slope or what has already moved.
- The days ahead are a weather model's forecast, issued when this record was signed; past days are reanalysis (ERA5) or that model's own analysis, not a rain gauge.
- The ranking compares totals with ERA5's at the same place. The forecast model and ERA5 are different models on different grids, and ERA5 is known to under-read short convective bursts, so a forecast total ranks high a little more easily than an observed one would.
- Signed rain series: `emem:fact:defi.zb55b.zihO.gAgA:a3x4jhhaiisr44mqjkxvel6zn5ustemztmyhhysprdgh635xkibq`.

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells (0.160 km² each) over a box 4.8 km a side. A cell counts when a clear pass reads at least 0.25 below the previous one in NDVI, the previous one was at least 0.4, and the next two passes stay at least half that drop below it: a missed cloud lasts one pass, a scar stays. Seasonal browning is gradual and does not count; harvest does, so this desk watches forests and slopes, not cropland.
- What it cannot tell apart from the series alone: a landslide from a burn or a clearing. The place says which it watches for; read a count as "vegetation lost", then look.
- Box: latitude 30.5334 to 30.5766, longitude 79.5400 to 79.5900.

### Pre-registration: Memory and fusion, replicated: do the memory-driven detectors hold on ten more tropical forests?

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

The memory-fusion experiment read only six of its ten forests, and there the fused version-2 detector was the only method to beat deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. This replication registers the same methods, word for word and hash for hash, on the four forests that experiment could not read and six more no experiment has scored, with each long read split into two date chunks so that more of them complete. Does each method beat the baseline, and do the registered comparisons and the stated false-alarm rate hold?

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Independent of every method: they read Sentinel-2, the reference reads Landsat.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2024 or 2025, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2023 (a 2023 clearing first seen in January 2024 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.
- `lab:memory_optical@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection (2026-10-29)). The cell's NBR remembered from its own year before the window (an annual harmonic and a robust spread), then a sequential test: each pass adds the capped log ratio of 'NBR 0.20 below the remembered value' against 'as remembered'; the timeline forks when evidence starts to build, and a change is confirmed at odds of 39 to 1 or the fork collapses. Its date is when the confirmed fork opened. Source blake3 `c9d911a504690c5d261e24ee2b06a23d1aced1bc681f27044a959be49ca2e68b`.
- `lab:memory_radar@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection on Sentinel-1 (2026-10-29)). The same memory and sequential test on the cell's Sentinel-1 VH backscatter alone, with 'disturbed' 2 dB below the remembered value (clearing removes the canopy's volume scattering; Reiche et al. 2018). Radar sees through cloud and haze. Source blake3 `9a67bfcc3f5d3941eaeb87d064a4c40a0f72f07412c6770d961c033352a47e3f`.
- `lab:memory_fusion@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion (2026-10-29)). One timeline per cell, fed by both sensors in date order: each Sentinel-2 NBR pass and each Sentinel-1 VH pass adds its capped log ratio against the cell's own remembered normal for that sensor, so an optical pass lost to cloud is replaced by a radar pass, and a hazy optical pass alone cannot confirm a change (Reiche et al. 2015, 2018). Source blake3 `52424db9f8de3dd49aa4a439cc55d3dafe4239387b9c0ffdd7ecf776f642e77e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory on Sentinel-2 (2026-10-29)). Five years of the cell's own NDVI, NBR and NDMI as its normal: a seasonal fit per band and a shrunk rank covariance across them. Each pass's evidence is the matched filter for the canopy-loss direction (NDVI, NBR and NDMI falling in the ratio 0.15 : 0.20 : 0.15) under that covariance, for losses of 1.5, 3 and 6 standard deviations along it, in parallel CUSUM charts. The alarm is calibrated on the cell's remembered noise to a 5% false-alarm chance over the window. Source blake3 `935bd44dcc4916e419a8dcc22481884db0c43822400aca5ccd33e1a0f1e60ce2`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory, Sentinel-1 and -2 (2026-10-29)). The same memory, filter and calibration with Sentinel-1 VH as a second sensor on the same timeline (a loss lowers VH), each sensor's noise replayed from its own memory. Source blake3 `1606d7bb91be6385d715f5912e9b45c1cdc7ad33a6aa382c6239040d470e08ba`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_fdr@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with false-discovery control (2026-10-29)). The fused statistic's p-value per cell, with Benjamini-Hochberg across a forest's cells at q = 0.10, so at most a tenth of the cells it flags are expected to be false. Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `4accd68a08f1756f2743961ac460af07582ad8f1396944a1f94102d9009d860e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_rel@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with neighbour relations (2026-10-29)). The fused p-value per cell, with the cell's neighbours as evidence: clearings spread, so a cell whose neighbours also depart from their memories is weighted up in a weighted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at q = 0.10 (Genovese, Roeder and Wasserman 2006). Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `fbcd9902c821f7fddebe23b811ea3d27ffc22675798df55629582893f905c1a8`.

#### The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best MCC on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is written up and fixed as a rule of its own, to be tested on sites none of this experiment's were.

#### Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

#### Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2026 can be 2025's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. MCC decides because it counts the stable forest a method left alone: on 29 October 2026 the F1 rule let a detector that flagged 74% of stable forest win where loss was common. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples of cells, seed 7) of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. Ten comparisons are registered beside it, each on the same cells by the same paired bootstrap of MCC: radar and optical against each other within version 1 (fusion minus optical, fusion minus radar), memory against a fixed seasonal threshold (memory_optical minus seasonal_loss_nbr, memory_fusion minus seasonal_loss_nbr), each version-2 upgrade against what it replaces (mv_optical minus memory_optical, mv_fusion minus memory_fusion, mv_fusion minus mv_optical), version 2 against the best fixed rule (mv_fusion minus seasonal_loss_nbr), relations against none (mv_fusion_rel minus mv_fusion_fdr) and site-level false-discovery control against per-cell calibration (mv_fusion_fdr minus mv_fusion). The calibrated methods state a 5% chance of flagging a stable cell over the window; the observed rate on stable cells is reported with a Wilson 95% interval, and calibration holds when the interval's lower end is at or under 5%. Every setting of every memory method was fixed before any of these forests was read.

#### Sites

- Apui, Amazonas (-7.600, -59.900), a box 4.8 km a side
- Equateur, DR Congo (0.000, 19.500), a box 4.8 km a side
- Ogooue-Ivindo, Gabon (0.500, 12.800), a box 4.8 km a side
- Kachin, Myanmar (25.500, 97.000), a box 4.8 km a side
- Itaituba, Para (-5.300, -56.500), a box 4.8 km a side
- Humaita, Amazonas (-7.600, -63.000), a box 4.8 km a side
- Juina, Mato Grosso (-11.400, -58.700), a box 4.8 km a side
- Sangha, Republic of Congo (1.600, 16.200), a box 4.8 km a side
- Aceh, Sumatra (4.300, 96.900), a box 4.8 km a side
- West Sepik, Papua New Guinea (-3.500, 141.500), a box 4.8 km a side

Code: emem-world `agents/lab.py`; every method above is named by the blake3 of its own source, so a rerun can prove it ran the same rule.


#### Status rule v2: methods are judged by all their evidence

---
kind: status_rule
rule: v2
effective: 2026-10-29
replaces: strict (every later experiment must win)
---
### Status rule v2: methods are judged by all their evidence

**What changed.** Until now a proposal was *replicated* only when every pre-registered experiment after its first win
also won, and *not replicated* after a single experiment that did not. From 29 October 2026 a method's status is
decided by all of its evidence:

- Counted: each MCC experiment on a site set disjoint from the earlier counted ones. A row that scored a search,
  rather than the rule the search picked, does not count for the rule.
- Fewer than three counted site sets: **proposed, awaiting replication** when the method won one and was
  significantly worse in none; otherwise **not shown better**.
- Three or more: the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects pooled MCC difference from the registry baseline.
  **Replicated** when its 95% lower bound is above zero and no counted experiment was significantly worse
  (interval wholly below zero); **replicated, forest-dependent** when, in addition, I² is 75% or more; **worse
  than the baseline** when its upper bound is below zero; otherwise **not shown better**.
- Every proposal note keeps the strict rule's verdict beside the new one.

**Why.** The strict rule demoted three methods on one experiment (`canopy-loss-memory-fusion-2024-2025-2026-10-29`)
that read six of its ten forests, after four consecutive wins for two of them. A rule that asks every experiment to
win makes *not replicated* certain for any method, however good, given enough experiments: it punishes running
them. Evidence synthesis is the standard answer.

**Disclosed.** The rule was adopted after the strict rule demoted those methods, by the owner's decision and in the
open. It applies to every method's record alike, and the notes that read the record print both verdicts. The code
is `lab.evidence_status` and `lab.random_effects` in emem-world `agents/lab.py`, source blake3 `acba2f5ce9ae3790e0e1b95bbf8c9c2b1f39635fba7cab8a26e14671618aebda`.

### Coast brief: Puducherry promenade, 2026-10-29 (COAST)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Is the beach along the Puducherry promenade coming back, and how fast?

#### Answer

No trend that the scatter allows (-8.3 m a year, 95% interval -16.8 to +0.1). Over 3.0 years of clear passes the sea reached a median of 1135 m into this 2.4 km box from its east edge; the Theil-Sen trend is -8.3 m a year of shore position (positive seaward), against a typical pass-to-pass scatter of 16 m.

| pass | sea width (m) | transects |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-02-08 | 1150 | 12 |
| 2026-02-18 | 1120 | 10 |
| 2026-02-28 | 1141 | 12 |
| 2026-03-07 | 1154 | 12 |
| 2026-03-20 | 1160 | 12 |
| 2026-04-14 | 1132 | 12 |
| 2026-04-29 | 1130 | 12 |
| 2026-06-28 | 1152 | 12 |
| 2026-08-27 | 1148 | 12 |
| 2026-09-06 | 1146 | 12 |
| 2026-10-03 | 1116 | 11 |
| 2026-10-11 | 1139 | 12 |

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells of 200 m over a box 2.4 km a side. Each cell's water fraction comes from its NDWI 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles (the share of pixels above 0, McFeeters 1996), so a shoreline moving a tenth of a cell shows. Each row running out to sea is a transect: the water counted from the sea edge until the first mostly-dry cell, so lagoons and flooded fields behind the beach do not count.
- Not corrected for tide, wave run-up or the season's sand cycle: that is most of the scatter, and the robust trend over many passes is what averages it out. A trend whose 95% interval (Sen 1968, from the ranks of the pairwise slopes) includes zero is reported as no trend.
- Box: latitude 11.9242 to 11.9458, longitude 79.8250 to 79.8470.

#### Check it yourself

- Signed series: `emem:fact:defi.zb487.zcb2e.jahi:6z7xrsdv2yxzu55vbyeucrxpupeq7eoa2mz2p4iwhiqv4qxrzbda`.
- Why this place is on the desk: a beach lost to erosion behind a seawall, where nourishment and a submerged reef aim to restore it.

#### Outlook: area median NDVI

- **0.76 on 2026-10-31** (80% band 0.64 to 0.88), 28 days ahead, by the anomaly method. Over 19 past cases in this series it erred by 0.081 on average; persistence (today's value) by 0.090, the season alone by 0.081; it does not beat both, so read it as no better than they are.

#### Outlook: area median NDMI
