### Pre-registration: Two references: does the ranking of methods hold when JRC TMF judges, not only Hansen?

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

Every result so far is agreement with Hansen, and on 4,391 tropical cells Hansen and JRC TMF agree on which cells lost forest at an MCC of only 0.39 to 0.48. If a method's lead over the registry rule is real and not an artefact of one reference's definition, it should hold when TMF judges, and on the cells where both agree. On ten tropical forests no experiment has scored, for loss in 2022 and 2023 (TMF ends in 2023), does each method beat deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1 under Hansen, under TMF, and on the agreed cells?

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Two independent references, scored separately. Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year (Landsat, any loss of tree cover) and JRC Tropical Moist Forest deforestation year (Landsat, conversion of moist tropical forest), each read through emem's band_raster for the same box. Hansen's 2000 tree cover is the forest mask for both.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2024 or 2025, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2023 (a 2023 clearing first seen in January 2024 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.
- `lab:memory_optical@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection (2026-10-29)). The cell's NBR remembered from its own year before the window (an annual harmonic and a robust spread), then a sequential test: each pass adds the capped log ratio of 'NBR 0.20 below the remembered value' against 'as remembered'; the timeline forks when evidence starts to build, and a change is confirmed at odds of 39 to 1 or the fork collapses. Its date is when the confirmed fork opened. Source blake3 `c9d911a504690c5d261e24ee2b06a23d1aced1bc681f27044a959be49ca2e68b`.
- `lab:memory_radar@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection on Sentinel-1 (2026-10-29)). The same memory and sequential test on the cell's Sentinel-1 VH backscatter alone, with 'disturbed' 2 dB below the remembered value (clearing removes the canopy's volume scattering; Reiche et al. 2018). Radar sees through cloud and haze. Source blake3 `9a67bfcc3f5d3941eaeb87d064a4c40a0f72f07412c6770d961c033352a47e3f`.
- `lab:memory_fusion@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion (2026-10-29)). One timeline per cell, fed by both sensors in date order: each Sentinel-2 NBR pass and each Sentinel-1 VH pass adds its capped log ratio against the cell's own remembered normal for that sensor, so an optical pass lost to cloud is replaced by a radar pass, and a hazy optical pass alone cannot confirm a change (Reiche et al. 2015, 2018). Source blake3 `52424db9f8de3dd49aa4a439cc55d3dafe4239387b9c0ffdd7ecf776f642e77e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory on Sentinel-2 (2026-10-29)). Five years of the cell's own NDVI, NBR and NDMI as its normal: a seasonal fit per band and a shrunk rank covariance across them. Each pass's evidence is the matched filter for the canopy-loss direction (NDVI, NBR and NDMI falling in the ratio 0.15 : 0.20 : 0.15) under that covariance, for losses of 1.5, 3 and 6 standard deviations along it, in parallel CUSUM charts. The alarm is calibrated on the cell's remembered noise to a 5% false-alarm chance over the window. Source blake3 `935bd44dcc4916e419a8dcc22481884db0c43822400aca5ccd33e1a0f1e60ce2`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory, Sentinel-1 and -2 (2026-10-29)). The same memory, filter and calibration with Sentinel-1 VH as a second sensor on the same timeline (a loss lowers VH), each sensor's noise replayed from its own memory. Source blake3 `1606d7bb91be6385d715f5912e9b45c1cdc7ad33a6aa382c6239040d470e08ba`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_fdr@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with false-discovery control (2026-10-29)). The fused statistic's p-value per cell, with Benjamini-Hochberg across a forest's cells at q = 0.10, so at most a tenth of the cells it flags are expected to be false. Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `4accd68a08f1756f2743961ac460af07582ad8f1396944a1f94102d9009d860e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_rel@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with neighbour relations (2026-10-29)). The fused p-value per cell, with the cell's neighbours as evidence: clearings spread, so a cell whose neighbours also depart from their memories is weighted up in a weighted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at q = 0.10 (Genovese, Roeder and Wasserman 2006). Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `fbcd9902c821f7fddebe23b811ea3d27ffc22675798df55629582893f905c1a8`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 2's fused memory and charts, scored continuously against the cell's own null, then decided across the forest under an empirical null: the cells together estimate the departure they all share this year, and a cell is flagged for what it shows beyond that, at a 5% false-alarm rate (Efron 2004). Returns (date, score, null scores); the experiment applies the forest's decision. Source blake3 `c69a7d9a5f1ca356d255304fd40a127cd5c993c3e21bb1eb3e83f80f1fdd0907`.

#### The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best MCC on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is written up and fixed as a rule of its own, to be tested on sites none of this experiment's were.

#### Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

#### Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2026 can be 2025's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. MCC decides because it counts the stable forest a method left alone: on 29 October 2026 the F1 rule let a detector that flagged 74% of stable forest win where loss was common. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples of cells, seed 7) of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. Hansen decides, as in every earlier experiment, and its result enters each method's record. Registered beside it: the same MCC and paired bootstrap against TMF's deforestation year, by the same cell rule with Hansen's forest mask, and on the cells where the two references give the same label. A method is robust to the reference when it beats the baseline under all three. One more comparison is registered: lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3 minus lab:memory_mv_fusion@2, whether judging each cell against what the forest's cells share this year (an empirical null) improves on judging it against its own memory alone; both state a 5% false-alarm rate, checked on the stable cells.

#### Sites

- Porto Velho north, Rondonia (-8.500, -63.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Paragominas, Para (-3.000, -47.400), a box 4.8 km a side
- Lacandona, Chiapas (16.600, -91.000), a box 4.8 km a side
- Pacaja, Para (-3.800, -50.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Imataca, Venezuela (7.500, -61.500), a box 4.8 km a side
- Choco, Colombia (6.000, -76.800), a box 4.8 km a side
- Palawan, Philippines (9.800, 118.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Olancho, Honduras (14.900, -85.900), a box 4.8 km a side
- Sabah, Borneo (5.200, 117.500), a box 4.8 km a side
- Dja, Cameroon (3.000, 12.800), a box 4.8 km a side

Code: emem-world `agents/lab.py`; every method above is named by the blake3 of its own source, so a rerun can prove it ran the same rule.

### Erratum to the pre-registration: Two references

Written at 2026-10-29T21:06Z, while the experiment reads its forests and before any of its results was computed or seen. The transparency log orders this note before the result note.

The plan (`/memories/by_attester/mujzmxes/research/experiments/canopy-loss-two-references-2022-2023-2026-10-29/plan.md`, file_cid `nppiqq7e6wznwzwpa4kfxuvele`) asks about loss in 2022 and 2023, and the run scores exactly that. Two of its paragraphs were copied from the 2024-2025 experiments and still name their years:

- **Labels** says a forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover "in 2024 or 2025", and STABLE when none did and none lost cover "in 2023". The run calls a forest cell LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2022 or 2023, and STABLE when none lost cover in 2022 or 2023 and none in 2021. Cells in between are left out and counted, as written.
- **Decision** says a method flags a cell for a loss it dates "from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31". The run counts dates from 2022-01-01 to 2024-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2024 can be 2023's).

Everything else is as registered: the question, the two references (TMF ends in 2023), the windows read (2021-01-01 to 2024-06-30, memory 2019-01-01 to 2020-12-31), the sites, the score (MCC) and every method's source. The years and dates the run uses were set in the experiment's parameters (`years` [2022, 2023], `adjacent` [2021], score window 2022-01-01 to 2024-03-31) before the plan was signed. The plan did not print those parameters, so this note states them.

From the next plan on, the lab refuses to register a plan whose labels or decision name a year or a date that its parameters do not contain.

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells (0.160 km² each) over a box 4.8 km a side. Seasonal browning is gradual and does not count; harvest does, so this desk watches forests and slopes, not cropland.
- What it cannot tell apart from the series alone: a landslide from a burn or a clearing. The place says which it watches for; read a count as "vegetation lost", then look.

#### Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2021 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

#### False alarms: stated in advance, then observed

Each of these methods calibrates its alarm on the cell's own remembered noise and states its chance of flagging a stable cell over the window before any data is read. Observed on this experiment's stable cells, with a Wilson 95% interval:

- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2`: stated 5%, observed 13 of 1062 (1.2%, 0.7% to 2.1%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2`: stated 5%, observed 19 of 1062 (1.8%, 1.1% to 2.8%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3`: stated 5%, observed 14 of 1062 (1.3%, 0.8% to 2.2%): calibrated.

### Agriculture-global brief: Winter wheat near Poltava, Ukraine, 2026-10-29 (AGENT B)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Has this autumn's winter wheat emerged, in how many fields, against last year?

#### Answer

99 cells are in the season under way, which peaked around **2026-07-17**. It has greened down (NDVI fell through half its amplitude and stayed down) in **25 of 99** by the pass of 2026-10-27. Green-down dates the end of the crop's growth: harvest follows it by days to weeks, so read this as how far the season has run, not as the harvest itself.
A year earlier, at 2025-10-27, 0 of the 70 cells whose season peaked at the same time had greened down.
A new season is greening (its season ended, or none was under way, and it has climbed at least 0.15 above its lowest point since) in 3 of 100 cells; a year earlier, 0.

#### What was studied

no mapped field polygons here (2 found), so a grid of 10 x 10 cells of about 140 m over 1.4 km stands in for fields: a cell can hold more than one field, so read its season as the dominant one. Their median seasonal NDVI swing is 0.61.

#### Crop seasons in the window, grouped by when they peaked

Groups are the dates most cells peak near (the modes of the peak dates); each counts a cell once per season. The crops are not named: the seasons come out of the data. Method: per cell: NDVI area median per pass (field_series fields mode); a pass reading more than 0.1 below both neighbours is left out (cloud the mask missed); 3-pass running median; peaks closer than 60 days are one season; per-season amplitude threshold 0.5 (TIMESAT; White et al. 1997), each side of a season judged on its own amplitude (at least 0.15); an end counts only if the curve stays under the line for 20 days.

| peak (median) | cells | started: median (middle half) | ended: median (middle half) | ended by 2026-10-27 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-07-24 | 69 | 2025-04-30 (2025-04-26..2025-05-18) | 2025-11-17 (2025-11-08..2025-11-17) | 30 |
| 2025-09-25 | 60 | 2025-05-18 (2025-04-30..2025-05-18) | 2025-11-17 (2025-11-08..2025-11-17) | 60 |
| 2026-07-17 | 99 | 2026-04-10 (2026-04-03..2026-04-24) | 2026-09-25 (2026-09-14..2026-09-30) | 20 |

The plan was published before any data was read: `/memories/by_attester/mujzmxes/research/experiments/canopy-loss-memory-fusion-replication-2024-2025-2026-10-29/plan.md` (file_cid `u24aifkusddf2zyyhoyhvygwtm`). #### Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2023 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

#### False alarms: stated in advance, then observed

Each of these methods calibrates its alarm on the cell's own remembered noise and states its chance of flagging a stable cell over the window before any data is read. Observed on this experiment's stable cells, with a Wilson 95% interval:

- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2`: stated 5%, observed 21 of 1175 (1.8%, 1.2% to 2.7%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2`: stated 5%, observed 18 of 1175 (1.5%, 1.0% to 2.4%): calibrated.

#### The search, scored on sites it never saw

32 variants of the seasonal rule were searched. For each site the variant with the best MCC on the other sites was applied to it; over all sites those out-of-sample picks score **MCC 0.030**, and their MCC minus the baseline's has a 95% interval of +0.038 to +0.176: the searched rule beats the registry baseline.

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells (0.160 km² each) over a box 4.8 km a side. A cell counts when a clear pass reads at least 0.27 below the previous one in NBR, the previous one was at least 0.3, and the next two passes stay at least half that drop below it: a missed cloud lasts one pass, a scar stays. Seasonal browning is gradual and does not count; harvest does, so this desk watches forests and slopes, not cropland. For fire the index is NBR and the drop is dNBR 0.27, moderate severity in Key & Benson (2006).
- What it cannot tell apart from the series alone: a landslide from a burn or a clearing. The place says which it watches for; read a count as "vegetation lost", then look.

### Pre-registration: Two optical sensors: does Landsat in the memory find loss that cloud hides from Sentinel-2?

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

Cloud is the limit on optical detection in the humid tropics: a cell can go months without a clear Sentinel-2 pass. Version 4 (lab:memory_hls_emp@4) puts Landsat 8 and 9 into the same optical memory as Sentinel-2, on Sentinel-2's scale by each cell's own remembered passes, with Sentinel-1 VH beside it; version 3 (lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3) is the same detector without Landsat. The forests are every one of the desk's site pool that no experiment has scored, that lies within 7 degrees of the equator, where cloud is most persistent, and whose cells lost forest in 2021 to 2023 by Hansen, the three years before the scored ones. Two experiments in October showed that a forest with no loss adds stable cells and no evidence. 13 forests were candidates and 9 qualified, with these counts of 400 m forest cells that lost 5% or more in 2021-2023: Kapuas Hulu, West Kalimantan 34 of 142; Lobaye, Central African Republic 34 of 144; San Martin, Peru 21 of 109; Sinoe, Liberia 16 of 144; Meta, Colombia 8 of 97; Altamira, Para 7 of 84; South Sumatra 5 of 21; Sankuru, DR Congo 3 of 144; Cavally, Cote d'Ivoire 1 of 144. The results speak for forests where loss was already under way. Does version 4 beat version 3, and does each method beat deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1? Each forest's count of clear Sentinel-2 and Landsat passes in the window is reported afterwards from the cached series, as a description that decides nothing.

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Not independent of the Landsat input of version 4: Hansen maps loss from Landsat too, so a gain of version 4 over version 3 may partly be agreement of one sensor with itself. The other methods read Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 only.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2024 or 2025, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2023 (a 2023 clearing first seen in January 2024 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.
- `lab:memory_optical@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection (2026-10-29)). The cell's NBR remembered from its own year before the window (an annual harmonic and a robust spread), then a sequential test: each pass adds the capped log ratio of 'NBR 0.20 below the remembered value' against 'as remembered'; the timeline forks when evidence starts to build, and a change is confirmed at odds of 39 to 1 or the fork collapses. Its date is when the confirmed fork opened. Source blake3 `c9d911a504690c5d261e24ee2b06a23d1aced1bc681f27044a959be49ca2e68b`.
- `lab:memory_radar@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection on Sentinel-1 (2026-10-29)). The same memory and sequential test on the cell's Sentinel-1 VH backscatter alone, with 'disturbed' 2 dB below the remembered value (clearing removes the canopy's volume scattering; Reiche et al. 2018). Radar sees through cloud and haze. Source blake3 `9a67bfcc3f5d3941eaeb87d064a4c40a0f72f07412c6770d961c033352a47e3f`.
- `lab:memory_fusion@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion (2026-10-29)). One timeline per cell, fed by both sensors in date order: each Sentinel-2 NBR pass and each Sentinel-1 VH pass adds its capped log ratio against the cell's own remembered normal for that sensor, so an optical pass lost to cloud is replaced by a radar pass, and a hazy optical pass alone cannot confirm a change (Reiche et al. 2015, 2018). Source blake3 `52424db9f8de3dd49aa4a439cc55d3dafe4239387b9c0ffdd7ecf776f642e77e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory on Sentinel-2 (2026-10-29)). Five years of the cell's own NDVI, NBR and NDMI as its normal: a seasonal fit per band and a shrunk rank covariance across them. Each pass's evidence is the matched filter for the canopy-loss direction (NDVI, NBR and NDMI falling in the ratio 0.15 : 0.20 : 0.15) under that covariance, for losses of 1.5, 3 and 6 standard deviations along it, in parallel CUSUM charts. The alarm is calibrated on the cell's remembered noise to a 5% false-alarm chance over the window. Source blake3 `935bd44dcc4916e419a8dcc22481884db0c43822400aca5ccd33e1a0f1e60ce2`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory, Sentinel-1 and -2 (2026-10-29)). The same memory, filter and calibration with Sentinel-1 VH as a second sensor on the same timeline (a loss lowers VH), each sensor's noise replayed from its own memory. Source blake3 `1606d7bb91be6385d715f5912e9b45c1cdc7ad33a6aa382c6239040d470e08ba`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_fdr@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with false-discovery control (2026-10-29)). The fused statistic's p-value per cell, with Benjamini-Hochberg across a forest's cells at q = 0.10, so at most a tenth of the cells it flags are expected to be false. Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `4accd68a08f1756f2743961ac460af07582ad8f1396944a1f94102d9009d860e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_rel@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with neighbour relations (2026-10-29)). The fused p-value per cell, with the cell's neighbours as evidence: clearings spread, so a cell whose neighbours also depart from their memories is weighted up in a weighted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at q = 0.10 (Genovese, Roeder and Wasserman 2006). Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `fbcd9902c821f7fddebe23b811ea3d27ffc22675798df55629582893f905c1a8`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 2's fused memory and charts, scored continuously against the cell's own null, then decided across the forest under an empirical null: the cells together estimate the departure they all share this year, and a cell is flagged for what it shows beyond that, at a 5% false-alarm rate (Efron 2004). Returns (date, score, null scores); the experiment applies the forest's decision. Source blake3 `c69a7d9a5f1ca356d255304fd40a127cd5c993c3e21bb1eb3e83f80f1fdd0907`.
- `lab:memory_hls_emp@4` (lab; emem methods lab, one optical memory from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9, with Sentinel-1, under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 3 with Landsat 8 and 9 in the same optical memory as Sentinel-2. Each cell puts Landsat on Sentinel-2's scale from its own remembered passes, then both sensors' passes form one record: one seasonal normal, one noise, one year offset per year, so a dry year that lowers both sensors is replayed once in the null and not twice. Where cloud is the limit, two optical sensors give about twice the clear looks. Sentinel-1 VH stays its own sensor. Decided across the forest at a 5% false-alarm rate, as version 3. Without Landsat passes it reads as version 3. Source blake3 `8427d374e8e799e061e8604811176749a6995da3868babacb21b56f83aa44868`.

#### The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best MCC on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is written up and fixed as a rule of its own, to be tested on sites none of this experiment's were.

#### Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

#### Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2026 can be 2025's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero, with forests as the resampled unit (2,000 resamples of the forests with replacement, each bringing all its cells, seed 7): a clearing is one event seen in many cells, and resampling cells counts it many times over. The interval with cells resampled is reported beside it and decides nothing. Three comparisons are registered beside it, on the same cells by the same paired bootstrap of MCC over forests: version 4 minus version 3 (the question: what Landsat adds), version 4 minus version 2 (lab:memory_mv_fusion@2) and version 4 minus the best fixed rule (lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1). Landsat adds skill when the interval of version 4 minus version 3 lies wholly above zero, and costs skill when wholly below. The calibrated methods state a 5% chance of flagging a stable cell over the window; the observed rate on stable cells is reported with a Wilson 95% interval, and calibration holds when the interval's lower end is at or under 5%. Every setting of every memory method was fixed before any of these forests was read.

#### Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2023 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

#### False alarms: stated in advance, then observed

Each of these methods calibrates its alarm on the cell's own remembered noise and states its chance of flagging a stable cell over the window before any data is read. Observed on this experiment's stable cells, with a Wilson 95% interval:

- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2`: stated 5%, observed 15 of 740 (2.0%, 1.2% to 3.3%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2`: stated 5%, observed 27 of 740 (3.6%, 2.5% to 5.3%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3`: stated 5%, observed 11 of 740 (1.5%, 0.8% to 2.6%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_hls_emp@4`: stated 5%, observed 10 of 740 (1.4%, 0.7% to 2.5%): calibrated.

#### The question

Is Lake Rakshastal frozen, and when did its ice form and go out last winter?

#### Answer

**100%** of the area read open water on the pass of 2026-10-17: about 49.0 km² of the 49.0 km² studied, from 35 of 49 cells the pass saw clearly.
In the same weeks of earlier years (5 passes within 15 days of the day of year) the median was 41%: +59 points this year.

#### Method

- Test per cell: NDMI below 0.25 on the cell median: at Lake Manasarovar open water read -0.31 to 0.11 on 18 clear passes in both seasons and ice 0.37 to 0.90 on 9, because ice and snow are bright in near infrared and dark in shortwave infrared, while sun glint lifts both. Passes the scene check calls suspect are kept: freezing and opening are sudden.
- Area: a grid of 7 x 7 cells, 1.00 km² each, over a box 7.0 km a side; a pass counts when it saw at least 60% of the cells through the cloud mask, and passes emem marks suspect are left out.

### Kailash-region brief: Lake Rakshastal, north basin, 2026-10-30 (KAILASH)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Is the north basin of Lake Rakshastal frozen, and does it freeze and open at the same time as the south basin?

#### Answer

**100%** of the area read open water on the pass of 2026-10-27: about 9.0 km² of the 9.0 km² studied, from 32 of 36 cells the pass saw clearly.
In the same weeks of earlier years (33 passes within 15 days of the day of year) the median was 100%: about the same.
Over the window the share ran from 0% on 2022-02-05 to 100% on 2021-11-27, across 366 usable passes.

Ice periods in the window (ice months only, at least half the lake off open water, two passes or more):

- **100% on 2026-11-24** (80% band 72% to 100%), 28 days ahead, by the anomaly method. Over 279 past cases in this series it erred by 15 points on average; persistence (today's value) by 24 points, the season alone by 13 points; it does not beat both, so read it as no better than they are.

#### Method

- Test per cell: NDMI below 0.50 on the cell median: over three years of both lakes, open water read up to 0.38 and ice from 0.62, because ice and snow are bright in near infrared and dark in shortwave infrared, while sun glint lifts both; thin wet ice at break-up reads as water. Passes the scene check calls suspect are kept: freezing and opening are sudden.
- Area: a grid of 6 x 6 cells, 0.25 km² each, over a box 3.0 km a side; a pass counts when it saw at least 60% of the cells through the cloud mask, and passes emem marks suspect are left out.
- Box: latitude 30.7415 to 30.7685, longitude 81.2063 to 81.2377.

### Pre-registration: Selection forests, 2022 and 2023: the earlier period of the method-selection experiment

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

The earlier period of `canopy-loss-method-selection-2022-2025`: each candidate's record here, against Hansen, chooses a method per forest before 2024 and 2025 are read. These forests are new to the lab, so this is also a set of forests in every method's evidence. Does each method beat deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1, with forests as the resampled unit, and does version 4 beat version 3? The forests are the unused forests of the desk's pool with the most 400 m forest cells that lost 5% or more in 2021 to 2023 by Hansen, read before either period: Sao Felix do Xingu, Para 42 of 144; Boca do Acre, Amazonas 40 of 137; Sud-Ubangi, DR Congo 40 of 141; Sagaing, Myanmar 13 of 141; Zambezia, Mozambique 13 of 127; Sarawak interior 12 of 144; Attapeu, Laos 11 of 59; Masoala, Madagascar 11 of 144; Cujubim, Rondonia 10 of 77.

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Not independent of the Landsat input of version 4: Hansen maps loss from Landsat too, so a gain of version 4 over version 3 may partly be agreement of one sensor with itself. The other methods read Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 only.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2022 or 2023, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2021 (a 2021 clearing first seen in January 2022 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.
- `lab:memory_optical@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection (2026-10-29)). The cell's NBR remembered from its own year before the window (an annual harmonic and a robust spread), then a sequential test: each pass adds the capped log ratio of 'NBR 0.20 below the remembered value' against 'as remembered'; the timeline forks when evidence starts to build, and a change is confirmed at odds of 39 to 1 or the fork collapses. Its date is when the confirmed fork opened. Source blake3 `c9d911a504690c5d261e24ee2b06a23d1aced1bc681f27044a959be49ca2e68b`.
- `lab:memory_radar@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection on Sentinel-1 (2026-10-29)). The same memory and sequential test on the cell's Sentinel-1 VH backscatter alone, with 'disturbed' 2 dB below the remembered value (clearing removes the canopy's volume scattering; Reiche et al. 2018). Radar sees through cloud and haze. Source blake3 `9a67bfcc3f5d3941eaeb87d064a4c40a0f72f07412c6770d961c033352a47e3f`.
- `lab:memory_fusion@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion (2026-10-29)). One timeline per cell, fed by both sensors in date order: each Sentinel-2 NBR pass and each Sentinel-1 VH pass adds its capped log ratio against the cell's own remembered normal for that sensor, so an optical pass lost to cloud is replaced by a radar pass, and a hazy optical pass alone cannot confirm a change (Reiche et al. 2015, 2018). Source blake3 `52424db9f8de3dd49aa4a439cc55d3dafe4239387b9c0ffdd7ecf776f642e77e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory on Sentinel-2 (2026-10-29)). Five years of the cell's own NDVI, NBR and NDMI as its normal: a seasonal fit per band and a shrunk rank covariance across them. Each pass's evidence is the matched filter for the canopy-loss direction (NDVI, NBR and NDMI falling in the ratio 0.15 : 0.20 : 0.15) under that covariance, for losses of 1.5, 3 and 6 standard deviations along it, in parallel CUSUM charts. The alarm is calibrated on the cell's remembered noise to a 5% false-alarm chance over the window. Source blake3 `935bd44dcc4916e419a8dcc22481884db0c43822400aca5ccd33e1a0f1e60ce2`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory, Sentinel-1 and -2 (2026-10-29)). The same memory, filter and calibration with Sentinel-1 VH as a second sensor on the same timeline (a loss lowers VH), each sensor's noise replayed from its own memory. Source blake3 `1606d7bb91be6385d715f5912e9b45c1cdc7ad33a6aa382c6239040d470e08ba`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_fdr@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with false-discovery control (2026-10-29)). The fused statistic's p-value per cell, with Benjamini-Hochberg across a forest's cells at q = 0.10, so at most a tenth of the cells it flags are expected to be false. Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `4accd68a08f1756f2743961ac460af07582ad8f1396944a1f94102d9009d860e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_rel@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with neighbour relations (2026-10-29)). The fused p-value per cell, with the cell's neighbours as evidence: clearings spread, so a cell whose neighbours also depart from their memories is weighted up in a weighted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at q = 0.10 (Genovese, Roeder and Wasserman 2006). Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `fbcd9902c821f7fddebe23b811ea3d27ffc22675798df55629582893f905c1a8`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 2's fused memory and charts, scored continuously against the cell's own null, then decided across the forest under an empirical null: the cells together estimate the departure they all share this year, and a cell is flagged for what it shows beyond that, at a 5% false-alarm rate (Efron 2004). Returns (date, score, null scores); the experiment applies the forest's decision. Source blake3 `c69a7d9a5f1ca356d255304fd40a127cd5c993c3e21bb1eb3e83f80f1fdd0907`.
- `lab:memory_hls_emp@4` (lab; emem methods lab, one optical memory from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9, with Sentinel-1, under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 3 with Landsat 8 and 9 in the same optical memory as Sentinel-2. Each cell puts Landsat on Sentinel-2's scale from its own remembered passes, then both sensors' passes form one record: one seasonal normal, one noise, one year offset per year, so a dry year that lowers both sensors is replayed once in the null and not twice. Where cloud is the limit, two optical sensors give about twice the clear looks. Sentinel-1 VH stays its own sensor. Decided across the forest at a 5% false-alarm rate, as version 3. Without Landsat passes it reads as version 3. Source blake3 `8427d374e8e799e061e8604811176749a6995da3868babacb21b56f83aa44868`.

#### The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best MCC on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is written up and fixed as a rule of its own, to be tested on sites none of this experiment's were.

#### Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

#### Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2022-01-01 to 2024-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2024 can be 2023's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero, with forests as the resampled unit (2,000 resamples of the forests with replacement, each bringing all its cells, seed 7): a clearing is one event seen in many cells, and resampling cells counts it many times over. The interval with cells resampled is reported beside it and decides nothing. Three comparisons are registered beside it, on the same cells by the same paired bootstrap of MCC over forests: version 4 minus version 3 (the question: what Landsat adds), version 4 minus version 2 (lab:memory_mv_fusion@2) and version 4 minus the best fixed rule (lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1). Landsat adds skill when the interval of version 4 minus version 3 lies wholly above zero, and costs skill when wholly below. The calibrated methods state a 5% chance of flagging a stable cell over the window; the observed rate on stable cells is reported with a Wilson 95% interval, and calibration holds when the interval's lower end is at or under 5%. Every setting of every memory method was fixed before any of these forests was read.

#### Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2021 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

#### False alarms: stated in advance, then observed

Each of these methods calibrates its alarm on the cell's own remembered noise and states its chance of flagging a stable cell over the window before any data is read. Observed on this experiment's stable cells, with a Wilson 95% interval:

- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2`: stated 5%, observed 0 of 187 (0.0%, 0.0% to 2.0%): calibrated.

#### The search, scored on sites it never saw

32 variants of the seasonal rule were searched. For each site the variant with the best MCC on the other sites was applied to it; over all sites those out-of-sample picks score **MCC 0.139**, and their MCC minus the baseline's has a 95% interval of -0.170 to +0.136: not shown better than the baseline.

Picks per held-out site:

- Sao Felix do Xingu, Para: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.25,from=0.3,post=45d]`
- Boca do Acre, Amazonas: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.15,from=0.4,post=30d]`
- Sud-Ubangi, DR Congo: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.15,from=0.3,post=30d]`

The variant best on all sites, which is what would be proposed: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.15,from=0.4,post=30d]`.

### Pre-registration: Context forests, 2022 and 2023: forests of the selection forests' climates, for the context policy

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

The context pool of `canopy-loss-method-selection-2022-2025`: ten forests the lab scored for 2024 and 2025 in earlier experiments, scored here for 2022 and 2023, so that the context policy reads only evidence dated before the period it is scored on. They are in the climate classes of the selection forests other than Am, which has five selection forests of its own: per class, the forests with eight or more 400 m forest cells that lost 5% or more in 2021 to 2023 by Hansen, up to five by loss, where a class had at least three (Cw had two and is left out, so the selection forest in Cw gets the global choice). Aw: Chiquitania, Santa Cruz, Bolivia 76 of 131; Bokeo, Laos 40 of 141; Lobaye, Central African Republic 34 of 144; Prey Lang, Cambodia 8 of 144; Sinop, Mato Grosso 8 of 77. Af: Jambi, Sumatra 96 of 144; Ketapang, West Kalimantan 69 of 141; Madre de Dios, Peru 61 of 130; Ituri rainforest, Congo basin 47 of 144; Caqueta, Colombia 27 of 144. These forests are in other experiments' evidence for 2024 and 2025, so they are not a new set of forests and this enters no method's status evidence. Does each method beat deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1 here, with forests as the resampled unit?

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Not independent of the Landsat input of version 4: Hansen maps loss from Landsat too, so a gain of version 4 over version 3 may partly be agreement of one sensor with itself. The other methods read Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 only.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2022 or 2023, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2021 (a 2021 clearing first seen in January 2022 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.
- `lab:memory_optical@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection (2026-10-29)). The cell's NBR remembered from its own year before the window (an annual harmonic and a robust spread), then a sequential test: each pass adds the capped log ratio of 'NBR 0.20 below the remembered value' against 'as remembered'; the timeline forks when evidence starts to build, and a change is confirmed at odds of 39 to 1 or the fork collapses. Its date is when the confirmed fork opened. Source blake3 `c9d911a504690c5d261e24ee2b06a23d1aced1bc681f27044a959be49ca2e68b`.
- `lab:memory_radar@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection on Sentinel-1 (2026-10-29)). The same memory and sequential test on the cell's Sentinel-1 VH backscatter alone, with 'disturbed' 2 dB below the remembered value (clearing removes the canopy's volume scattering; Reiche et al. 2018). Radar sees through cloud and haze. Source blake3 `9a67bfcc3f5d3941eaeb87d064a4c40a0f72f07412c6770d961c033352a47e3f`.
- `lab:memory_fusion@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion (2026-10-29)). One timeline per cell, fed by both sensors in date order: each Sentinel-2 NBR pass and each Sentinel-1 VH pass adds its capped log ratio against the cell's own remembered normal for that sensor, so an optical pass lost to cloud is replaced by a radar pass, and a hazy optical pass alone cannot confirm a change (Reiche et al. 2015, 2018). Source blake3 `52424db9f8de3dd49aa4a439cc55d3dafe4239387b9c0ffdd7ecf776f642e77e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory on Sentinel-2 (2026-10-29)). Five years of the cell's own NDVI, NBR and NDMI as its normal: a seasonal fit per band and a shrunk rank covariance across them. Each pass's evidence is the matched filter for the canopy-loss direction (NDVI, NBR and NDMI falling in the ratio 0.15 : 0.20 : 0.15) under that covariance, for losses of 1.5, 3 and 6 standard deviations along it, in parallel CUSUM charts. The alarm is calibrated on the cell's remembered noise to a 5% false-alarm chance over the window. Source blake3 `935bd44dcc4916e419a8dcc22481884db0c43822400aca5ccd33e1a0f1e60ce2`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory, Sentinel-1 and -2 (2026-10-29)). The same memory, filter and calibration with Sentinel-1 VH as a second sensor on the same timeline (a loss lowers VH), each sensor's noise replayed from its own memory. Source blake3 `1606d7bb91be6385d715f5912e9b45c1cdc7ad33a6aa382c6239040d470e08ba`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_fdr@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with false-discovery control (2026-10-29)). The fused statistic's p-value per cell, with Benjamini-Hochberg across a forest's cells at q = 0.10, so at most a tenth of the cells it flags are expected to be false. Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `4accd68a08f1756f2743961ac460af07582ad8f1396944a1f94102d9009d860e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_rel@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with neighbour relations (2026-10-29)). The fused p-value per cell, with the cell's neighbours as evidence: clearings spread, so a cell whose neighbours also depart from their memories is weighted up in a weighted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at q = 0.10 (Genovese, Roeder and Wasserman 2006). Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `fbcd9902c821f7fddebe23b811ea3d27ffc22675798df55629582893f905c1a8`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 2's fused memory and charts, scored continuously against the cell's own null, then decided across the forest under an empirical null: the cells together estimate the departure they all share this year, and a cell is flagged for what it shows beyond that, at a 5% false-alarm rate (Efron 2004). Returns (date, score, null scores); the experiment applies the forest's decision. Source blake3 `c69a7d9a5f1ca356d255304fd40a127cd5c993c3e21bb1eb3e83f80f1fdd0907`.
- `lab:memory_hls_emp@4` (lab; emem methods lab, one optical memory from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9, with Sentinel-1, under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 3 with Landsat 8 and 9 in the same optical memory as Sentinel-2. Each cell puts Landsat on Sentinel-2's scale from its own remembered passes, then both sensors' passes form one record: one seasonal normal, one noise, one year offset per year, so a dry year that lowers both sensors is replayed once in the null and not twice. Where cloud is the limit, two optical sensors give about twice the clear looks. Sentinel-1 VH stays its own sensor. Decided across the forest at a 5% false-alarm rate, as version 3. Without Landsat passes it reads as version 3. Source blake3 `8427d374e8e799e061e8604811176749a6995da3868babacb21b56f83aa44868`.

#### The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best MCC on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is written up and fixed as a rule of its own, to be tested on sites none of this experiment's were.

#### Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

#### Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2022-01-01 to 2024-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2024 can be 2023's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero, with forests as the resampled unit (2,000 resamples of the forests with replacement, each bringing all its cells, seed 7): a clearing is one event seen in many cells, and resampling cells counts it many times over. The interval with cells resampled is reported beside it and decides nothing. Three comparisons are registered beside it, on the same cells by the same paired bootstrap of MCC over forests: version 4 minus version 3 (the question: what Landsat adds), version 4 minus version 2 (lab:memory_mv_fusion@2) and version 4 minus the best fixed rule (lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1). Landsat adds skill when the interval of version 4 minus version 3 lies wholly above zero, and costs skill when wholly below. The calibrated methods state a 5% chance of flagging a stable cell over the window; the observed rate on stable cells is reported with a Wilson 95% interval, and calibration holds when the interval's lower end is at or under 5%. Every setting of every memory method was fixed before any of these forests was read.

#### Sites

- Chiquitania, Santa Cruz, Bolivia (-16.300, -61.500), a box 4.8 km a side
- Bokeo, Laos (20.300, 100.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Lobaye, Central African Republic (3.700, 17.800), a box 4.8 km a side
- Prey Lang, Cambodia (13.200, 105.400), a box 4.8 km a side
- Sinop, Mato Grosso (-11.900, -55.300), a box 4.8 km a side
- Jambi, Sumatra (-1.600, 103.000), a box 4.8 km a side
- Ketapang, West Kalimantan (-1.900, 110.300), a box 4.8 km a side
- Madre de Dios, Peru (-12.600, -70.100), a box 4.8 km a side
- Ituri rainforest, Congo basin (1.400, 28.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Caqueta, Colombia (1.000, -74.500), a box 4.8 km a side

#### Method

- Test per cell: NDMI below 0.50 on the cell median: over three years of both lakes, open water read up to 0.38 and ice from 0.62, because ice and snow are bright in near infrared and dark in shortwave infrared, while sun glint lifts both; thin wet ice at break-up reads as water. Passes the scene check calls suspect are kept: freezing and opening are sudden.
- Area: a grid of 6 x 6 cells, 0.36 km² each, over a box 3.6 km a side; a pass counts when it saw at least 60% of the cells through the cloud mask, and passes emem marks suspect are left out.

#### Clearings found, by size

Hansen draws each clearing as 8-connected 30 m pixels that lost cover in the scored years (forest in 2000). #### Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2021 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

#### False alarms: stated in advance, then observed

Each of these methods calibrates its alarm on the cell's own remembered noise and states its chance of flagging a stable cell over the window before any data is read. Observed on this experiment's stable cells, with a Wilson 95% interval:

- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2`: stated 5%, observed 16 of 640 (2.5%, 1.5% to 4.0%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2`: stated 5%, observed 8 of 640 (1.2%, 0.6% to 2.4%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3`: stated 5%, observed 6 of 640 (0.9%, 0.4% to 2.0%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_hls_emp@4`: stated 5%, observed 8 of 640 (1.2%, 0.6% to 2.4%): calibrated.

#### Registered comparisons

Each pair on the same cells, MCC, 95% paired-bootstrap interval:

- lab:memory_hls_emp@4 minus lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3: -0.066 to +0.081 (no clear difference)
- lab:memory_hls_emp@4 minus lab:memory_mv_fusion@2: -0.072 to +0.067 (no clear difference)
- lab:memory_hls_emp@4 minus lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1: +0.022 to +0.438 (first better)

#### Does the temporal cloud screen help?

Each detector run on screened series against the same detector unscreened, same cells:

| detector | MCC unscreened | MCC screened | difference, 95% interval | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `desk:vegetation_loss@1` | 0.208 | 0.144 | -0.111 to -0.017 | hurts |
| `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` | 0.177 | 0.193 | -0.036 to +0.068 | no clear effect |
| `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` | 0.049 | 0.107 | +0.016 to +0.099 | helps |
| `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` | 0.083 | 0.149 | -0.000 to +0.137 | no clear effect |
| `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` | 0.117 | 0.166 | -0.017 to +0.113 | no clear effect |

#### The search, scored on sites it never saw

32 variants of the seasonal rule were searched. For each site the variant with the best MCC on the other sites was applied to it; over all sites those out-of-sample picks score **MCC 0.185**, and their MCC minus the baseline's has a 95% interval of -0.002 to +0.137: not shown better than the baseline.

Picks per held-out site:

- Chiquitania, Santa Cruz, Bolivia: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.15,from=0.4,post=45d]`
- Bokeo, Laos: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.15,from=0.4,post=45d]`
- Lobaye, Central African Republic: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.30,from=0.4,post=45d]`
- Prey Lang, Cambodia: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.30,from=0.4,post=45d]`
- Sinop, Mato Grosso: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.30,from=0.3,post=45d]`
- Jambi, Sumatra: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.15,from=0.3,post=45d]`
- Ketapang, West Kalimantan: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.30,from=0.4,post=45d]`
- Madre de Dios, Peru: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.30,from=0.4,post=45d]`
- Ituri rainforest, Congo basin: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.30,from=0.4,post=45d]`
- Caqueta, Colombia: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.30,from=0.4,post=45d]`

The variant best on all sites, which is what would be proposed: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.30,from=0.4,post=45d]`.

### Flood brief: Mundakkai slopes, Wayanad, 2026-10-30 (SENTINEL-1)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Has fresh bare ground opened on these slopes, where and when?

#### Answer

Landslide rain watch low; 90-day rain severely dry (z -1.6); no new fresh bare ground on the slopes (landslide scars) in the last 60 days (to 2026-10-12); window total 11 cells, most in 2025-09.

| month the loss was seen | cells | km² |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-05 | 1 | 0.16 |
| 2024-10 | 1 | 0.16 |
| 2025-05 | 1 | 0.16 |
| 2025-09 | 3 | 0.48 |
| 2025-10 | 3 | 0.48 |
| 2025-11 | 2 | 0.32 |

The largest drops:

- cell r11c07: NDVI 0.83 on 2025-05-07, 0.27 on 2025-09-02, and still down after
- cell r02c00: NDVI 0.77 on 2025-06-04, 0.32 on 2025-10-07, and still down after

- cell r00c01: NDVI 0.81 on 2025-10-12, 0.49 on 2025-11-03, and still down after
