#### Rain behind and ahead

- Last 7 days (to 2026-10-29): **54 mm**, at percentile 48 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Last 30 days (to 2026-10-29): **257 mm**, at percentile 39 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Last 90 days (to 2026-10-29): **635 mm**, at percentile 5 of these weeks since 1996 (severely dry).
- Next 3 days (forecast from 2026-10-30): **5 mm**, at percentile 19 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Next 7 days (forecast from 2026-10-30): **61 mm**, at percentile 62 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Next 14 days (forecast from 2026-10-30): **90 mm**, at percentile 47 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- **Landslide rain watch: low.** No total meets both tests. A watch is raised when a 3- or 7-day total, past or forecast, is above the global minimum for triggering shallow landslides (Guzzetti et al. 2008: 24 mm over 3 days, 39 mm over 7) and among the wettest 5% (elevated) or 1% (high) of those weeks since the climatology began. It reads rain only, not soil, slope or what has already moved.
- The days ahead are a weather model's forecast, issued when this record was signed; past days are reanalysis (ERA5) or that model's own analysis, not a rain gauge.
- The ranking compares totals with ERA5's at the same place. The forecast model and ERA5 are different models on different grids, and ERA5 is known to under-read short convective bursts, so a forecast total ranks high a little more easily than an observed one would.
- Signed rain series: `emem:fact:defi.zb482.zbb2d.vIwo:gywme7vvuxnuawrvofuo47mjoqx32tricp7lrzukket7cwsmaqsq`.

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells (0.160 km² each) over a box 4.8 km a side. A cell counts when a clear pass reads at least 0.25 below the previous one in NDVI, the previous one was at least 0.4, and the next two passes stay at least half that drop below it: a missed cloud lasts one pass, a scar stays. Seasonal browning is gradual and does not count; harvest does, so this desk watches forests and slopes, not cropland.
- What it cannot tell apart from the series alone: a landslide from a burn or a clearing. The place says which it watches for; read a count as "vegetation lost", then look.
- Box: latitude 11.4684 to 11.5116, longitude 76.1280 to 76.1720.

### Pre-registration: Method selection: can the lab tell which method suits each forest, from its own earlier record or from forests of its climate?

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

Can an agent discover that the method it trusted is wrong for a forest, choose a better one on independent evidence, and let another agent verify the whole decision? Each candidate's 2022-2023 record against Hansen, in `canopy-loss-selection-forests-2022-2023` and in a pool of other forests of the same climates, `canopy-loss-context-forests-2022-2023`, chooses a method per forest; each choice is signed as decision@1 before 2024-2025 is read, in `canopy-loss-selection-forests-2024-2025`, which then scores them. Does choosing per forest, by the forest's own record or by the record of forests of its climate, beat the method best on average, and is the champion worse where its earlier record flagged it? The forests are the unused forests of the desk's pool with the most 400 m forest cells that lost 5% or more in 2021 to 2023 by Hansen, read before either period: Sao Felix do Xingu, Para 42 of 144; Boca do Acre, Amazonas 40 of 137; Sud-Ubangi, DR Congo 40 of 141; Sagaing, Myanmar 13 of 141; Zambezia, Mozambique 13 of 127; Sarawak interior 12 of 144; Attapeu, Laos 11 of 59; Masoala, Madagascar 11 of 144; Cujubim, Rondonia 10 of 77.

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Not independent of the Landsat input of version 4: Hansen maps loss from Landsat too, so a gain of version 4 over version 3 may partly be agreement of one sensor with itself. The other methods read Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 only.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2024 or 2025, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2023 (a 2023 clearing first seen in January 2024 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.
- `lab:memory_optical@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection (2026-10-29)). The cell's NBR remembered from its own year before the window (an annual harmonic and a robust spread), then a sequential test: each pass adds the capped log ratio of 'NBR 0.20 below the remembered value' against 'as remembered'; the timeline forks when evidence starts to build, and a change is confirmed at odds of 39 to 1 or the fork collapses. Its date is when the confirmed fork opened. Source blake3 `c9d911a504690c5d261e24ee2b06a23d1aced1bc681f27044a959be49ca2e68b`.
- `lab:memory_radar@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection on Sentinel-1 (2026-10-29)). The same memory and sequential test on the cell's Sentinel-1 VH backscatter alone, with 'disturbed' 2 dB below the remembered value (clearing removes the canopy's volume scattering; Reiche et al. 2018). Radar sees through cloud and haze. Source blake3 `9a67bfcc3f5d3941eaeb87d064a4c40a0f72f07412c6770d961c033352a47e3f`.
- `lab:memory_fusion@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion (2026-10-29)). One timeline per cell, fed by both sensors in date order: each Sentinel-2 NBR pass and each Sentinel-1 VH pass adds its capped log ratio against the cell's own remembered normal for that sensor, so an optical pass lost to cloud is replaced by a radar pass, and a hazy optical pass alone cannot confirm a change (Reiche et al. 2015, 2018). Source blake3 `52424db9f8de3dd49aa4a439cc55d3dafe4239387b9c0ffdd7ecf776f642e77e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory on Sentinel-2 (2026-10-29)). Five years of the cell's own NDVI, NBR and NDMI as its normal: a seasonal fit per band and a shrunk rank covariance across them. Each pass's evidence is the matched filter for the canopy-loss direction (NDVI, NBR and NDMI falling in the ratio 0.15 : 0.20 : 0.15) under that covariance, for losses of 1.5, 3 and 6 standard deviations along it, in parallel CUSUM charts. The alarm is calibrated on the cell's remembered noise to a 5% false-alarm chance over the window. Source blake3 `935bd44dcc4916e419a8dcc22481884db0c43822400aca5ccd33e1a0f1e60ce2`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory, Sentinel-1 and -2 (2026-10-29)). The same memory, filter and calibration with Sentinel-1 VH as a second sensor on the same timeline (a loss lowers VH), each sensor's noise replayed from its own memory. Source blake3 `1606d7bb91be6385d715f5912e9b45c1cdc7ad33a6aa382c6239040d470e08ba`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_fdr@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with false-discovery control (2026-10-29)). The fused statistic's p-value per cell, with Benjamini-Hochberg across a forest's cells at q = 0.10, so at most a tenth of the cells it flags are expected to be false. Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `4accd68a08f1756f2743961ac460af07582ad8f1396944a1f94102d9009d860e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_rel@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with neighbour relations (2026-10-29)). The fused p-value per cell, with the cell's neighbours as evidence: clearings spread, so a cell whose neighbours also depart from their memories is weighted up in a weighted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at q = 0.10 (Genovese, Roeder and Wasserman 2006). Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `fbcd9902c821f7fddebe23b811ea3d27ffc22675798df55629582893f905c1a8`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 2's fused memory and charts, scored continuously against the cell's own null, then decided across the forest under an empirical null: the cells together estimate the departure they all share this year, and a cell is flagged for what it shows beyond that, at a 5% false-alarm rate (Efron 2004). Returns (date, score, null scores); the experiment applies the forest's decision. Source blake3 `c69a7d9a5f1ca356d255304fd40a127cd5c993c3e21bb1eb3e83f80f1fdd0907`.
- `lab:memory_hls_emp@4` (lab; emem methods lab, one optical memory from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9, with Sentinel-1, under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 3 with Landsat 8 and 9 in the same optical memory as Sentinel-2. Each cell puts Landsat on Sentinel-2's scale from its own remembered passes, then both sensors' passes form one record: one seasonal normal, one noise, one year offset per year, so a dry year that lowers both sensors is replayed once in the null and not twice. Where cloud is the limit, two optical sensors give about twice the clear looks. Sentinel-1 VH stays its own sensor. Decided across the forest at a 5% false-alarm rate, as version 3. Without Landsat passes it reads as version 3. Source blake3 `8427d374e8e799e061e8604811176749a6995da3868babacb21b56f83aa44868`.

#### Policies

The earlier record is every forest scored for 2022 and 2023 in `canopy-loss-selection-forests-2022-2023` (these forests) and in `canopy-loss-context-forests-2022-2023` (other forests of the same climates), and every policy reads all of it. P0, global: the candidate with the highest mean MCC over the forests of the earlier record with five or more loss cells. P1, local: at each forest, the candidate with the highest MCC shrunk towards its mean by empirical Bayes (weight tau2 / (tau2 + v): tau2 the DerSimonian-Laird between-forest variance, v the forest's sampling variance with cells resampled; a forest with fewer than five loss cells keeps the mean). P2, context: at each forest, the candidate with the highest mean MCC over the other forests of the earlier record in the same climate class (the first two letters of the Koppen class at the box centre, a signed emem fact) that have five or more loss cells; with fewer than three such forests, the global choice. P2 never reads the forest's own record, so it is the choice an agent can make at a forest it has never scored. P3, abstaining: P1 when the chosen candidate's shrunk lower bound (estimate minus 1.96 standard errors) exceeds the registry rule's shrunk estimate, else no choice. The champion is flagged wrong at a forest when its own 2022-2023 MCC there is more than 1.96 of its standard errors below its mean.

#### Metric and decision rule

The later period is scored like the two-optical-sensor experiment: a cell is flagged when a method dates a loss from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31, and LOSS and STABLE are pooled across forests. Each forest is judged by the method each policy chose for it. The local policy beats the global one when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of their MCC difference, with forests as the resampled unit (2,000 resamples, seed 7), lies wholly above zero. The context policy is compared with the global one in the same way, a second registered comparison with its own interval; neither comparison is adjusted for the other, and the number of forests where P2 chose other than P0 is reported beside it. The abstaining policy is reported with the number of forests it chose at, and its MCC beside the global champion's on those forests. The champion is counted as wrong where flagged when its later-period MCC at a flagged forest is below its mean over the forests with loss; the count is reported and decides nothing.

### Pre-registration: Selection forests, 2024 and 2025: the later period of the method-selection experiment

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

#### Question

The later period of `canopy-loss-method-selection-2022-2025`, read only after its decisions were signed, to score them. The same forests as `canopy-loss-selection-forests-2022-2023`, so not a new set of forests: it enters no method's evidence for its status.

#### Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Not independent of the Landsat input of version 4: Hansen maps loss from Landsat too, so a gain of version 4 over version 3 may partly be agreement of one sensor with itself. The other methods read Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 only.

#### Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2024 or 2025, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2023 (a 2023 clearing first seen in January 2024 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

#### Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:seasonal_canopy_loss@1` (lab; picked by the methods lab search under MCC, canopy-loss-mcc-replication (2026-10-29)). The search's pick on all seven sites of the MCC replication, fixed so that later experiments test this one rule rather than the search: NBR over the 45 days from t at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Its only score so far is the search's out-of-sample one, which measures the search, not this rule. Source blake3 `908ffad5ce9e619f31bebcc93b35f26197396d9ea95b8755e43270a83cf30d08`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.
- `lab:memory_optical@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection (2026-10-29)). The cell's NBR remembered from its own year before the window (an annual harmonic and a robust spread), then a sequential test: each pass adds the capped log ratio of 'NBR 0.20 below the remembered value' against 'as remembered'; the timeline forks when evidence starts to build, and a change is confirmed at odds of 39 to 1 or the fork collapses. Its date is when the confirmed fork opened. Source blake3 `c9d911a504690c5d261e24ee2b06a23d1aced1bc681f27044a959be49ca2e68b`.
- `lab:memory_radar@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven detection on Sentinel-1 (2026-10-29)). The same memory and sequential test on the cell's Sentinel-1 VH backscatter alone, with 'disturbed' 2 dB below the remembered value (clearing removes the canopy's volume scattering; Reiche et al. 2018). Radar sees through cloud and haze. Source blake3 `9a67bfcc3f5d3941eaeb87d064a4c40a0f72f07412c6770d961c033352a47e3f`.
- `lab:memory_fusion@1` (lab; emem methods lab, memory-driven Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion (2026-10-29)). One timeline per cell, fed by both sensors in date order: each Sentinel-2 NBR pass and each Sentinel-1 VH pass adds its capped log ratio against the cell's own remembered normal for that sensor, so an optical pass lost to cloud is replaced by a radar pass, and a hazy optical pass alone cannot confirm a change (Reiche et al. 2015, 2018). Source blake3 `52424db9f8de3dd49aa4a439cc55d3dafe4239387b9c0ffdd7ecf776f642e77e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory on Sentinel-2 (2026-10-29)). Five years of the cell's own NDVI, NBR and NDMI as its normal: a seasonal fit per band and a shrunk rank covariance across them. Each pass's evidence is the matched filter for the canopy-loss direction (NDVI, NBR and NDMI falling in the ratio 0.15 : 0.20 : 0.15) under that covariance, for losses of 1.5, 3 and 6 standard deviations along it, in parallel CUSUM charts. The alarm is calibrated on the cell's remembered noise to a 5% false-alarm chance over the window. Source blake3 `935bd44dcc4916e419a8dcc22481884db0c43822400aca5ccd33e1a0f1e60ce2`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate calibrated memory, Sentinel-1 and -2 (2026-10-29)). The same memory, filter and calibration with Sentinel-1 VH as a second sensor on the same timeline (a loss lowers VH), each sensor's noise replayed from its own memory. Source blake3 `1606d7bb91be6385d715f5912e9b45c1cdc7ad33a6aa382c6239040d470e08ba`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_fdr@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with false-discovery control (2026-10-29)). The fused statistic's p-value per cell, with Benjamini-Hochberg across a forest's cells at q = 0.10, so at most a tenth of the cells it flags are expected to be false. Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `4accd68a08f1756f2743961ac460af07582ad8f1396944a1f94102d9009d860e`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_rel@2` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory with neighbour relations (2026-10-29)). The fused p-value per cell, with the cell's neighbours as evidence: clearings spread, so a cell whose neighbours also depart from their memories is weighted up in a weighted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at q = 0.10 (Genovese, Roeder and Wasserman 2006). Returns (date, p); the experiment applies the procedure per site. Source blake3 `fbcd9902c821f7fddebe23b811ea3d27ffc22675798df55629582893f905c1a8`.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3` (lab; emem methods lab, multivariate memory under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 2's fused memory and charts, scored continuously against the cell's own null, then decided across the forest under an empirical null: the cells together estimate the departure they all share this year, and a cell is flagged for what it shows beyond that, at a 5% false-alarm rate (Efron 2004). Returns (date, score, null scores); the experiment applies the forest's decision. Source blake3 `c69a7d9a5f1ca356d255304fd40a127cd5c993c3e21bb1eb3e83f80f1fdd0907`.
- `lab:memory_hls_emp@4` (lab; emem methods lab, one optical memory from Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9, with Sentinel-1, under a forest-wide empirical null (2026-10-29)). Version 3 with Landsat 8 and 9 in the same optical memory as Sentinel-2. Each cell puts Landsat on Sentinel-2's scale from its own remembered passes, then both sensors' passes form one record: one seasonal normal, one noise, one year offset per year, so a dry year that lowers both sensors is replayed once in the null and not twice. Where cloud is the limit, two optical sensors give about twice the clear looks. Sentinel-1 VH stays its own sensor. Decided across the forest at a 5% false-alarm rate, as version 3. Without Landsat passes it reads as version 3. Source blake3 `8427d374e8e799e061e8604811176749a6995da3868babacb21b56f83aa44868`.

#### The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best MCC on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is written up and fixed as a rule of its own, to be tested on sites none of this experiment's were.

#### Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

#### Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2026 can be 2025's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero, with forests as the resampled unit (2,000 resamples of the forests with replacement, each bringing all its cells, seed 7): a clearing is one event seen in many cells, and resampling cells counts it many times over. The interval with cells resampled is reported beside it and decides nothing. Three comparisons are registered beside it, on the same cells by the same paired bootstrap of MCC over forests: version 4 minus version 3 (the question: what Landsat adds), version 4 minus version 2 (lab:memory_mv_fusion@2) and version 4 minus the best fixed rule (lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1). Landsat adds skill when the interval of version 4 minus version 3 lies wholly above zero, and costs skill when wholly below. The calibrated methods state a 5% chance of flagging a stable cell over the window; the observed rate on stable cells is reported with a Wilson 95% interval, and calibration holds when the interval's lower end is at or under 5%. Every setting of every memory method was fixed before any of these forests was read.

#### Sites

- Sao Felix do Xingu, Para (-6.800, -52.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Boca do Acre, Amazonas (-8.700, -67.400), a box 4.8 km a side
- Sud-Ubangi, DR Congo (3.300, 19.500), a box 4.8 km a side

- Zambezia, Mozambique (-16.500, 37.000), a box 4.8 km a side

### Agriculture-global brief: Nile delta fields near Tanta, 2026-10-30 (AGENT B)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

How many crops do these fields grow in a year, and where is the current one?

#### Answer

14 fields are in the season under way, which peaked around **2026-07-31**. It has greened down (NDVI fell through half its amplitude and stayed down) in **14 of 14** by the pass of 2026-10-29. Green-down dates the end of the crop's growth: harvest follows it by days to weeks, so read this as how far the season has run, not as the harvest itself.
Like for like, over the 14 fields that also had a season peaking at the same time a year earlier: 14 have greened down by 2026-10-29, and 14 had by 2025-10-29.
A new season is greening (its season ended, or none was under way, and it has climbed at least 0.15 above its lowest point since) in 1 of 17 fields; a year earlier, 1.

**Yield outlook (season vigour).** The green each field has built so far this season (NDVI accumulated above its starting level, from its lowest point of the last 150 days to 2026-10-29) against the same calendar span a year earlier: the median field is at **1.30x** last year's, and 6 of 10 are above it. Season-integrated NDVI tracks yield in many crops, so this says which way the harvest leans against last year; it is not tonnes per hectare. 1 fields were left out because the two seasons were not seen on a similar number of clear passes.

#### What was studied

17 real field polygons within about 1.4 km (the largest, at least 1,000 m² each; Fields of The World, CC-BY-4.0). Their median seasonal NDVI swing is 0.80.

#### Crop seasons in the window, grouped by when they peaked

Groups are the dates most fields peak near (the modes of the peak dates); each counts a field once per season. The crops are not named: the seasons come out of the data. Method: per field: NDVI area median per pass (field_series fields mode); a pass reading more than 0.1 below both neighbours is left out (cloud the mask missed); 3-pass running median; peaks closer than 60 days are one season; per-season amplitude threshold 0.5 (TIMESAT; White et al. 1997), each side of a season judged on its own amplitude (at least 0.15); an end counts only if the curve stays under the line for 20 days.

### Wildlife brief: Boma-Jonglei antelope range, South Sudan, 2026-10-30 (WILDLIFE)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Where is the freshest grazing across the Boma-Jonglei landscape, for the kob and tiang migration?

#### Answer

Freshest grazing at Sudd edge (NDVI 0.66, +0.08 in 30 days); drying fastest at Badingilo (-0.17). Herds that follow green grass are likeliest to move toward the areas at the top of this table; it is an inference from forage, not a sighting.

| area | pass | NDVI | change in 30 days | against the same weeks of earlier years |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sudd edge | 2026-10-30 | 0.66 | +0.08 | -0.04 |
| Boma plateau | 2026-10-30 | 0.61 | +0.01 | -0.06 |
| Pibor | 2026-07-17 | 0.59 | -0.02 | n/a |
| Jonglei plains | 2026-10-30 | 0.62 | -0.02 | -0.02 |
| Kenamuke swamp | 2026-10-30 | 0.22 | -0.04 | -0.28 |
| Badingilo | 2026-10-30 | 0.42 | -0.17 | -0.20 |

#### Method

- One signed field_series per area (boxes about 4.8 km a side), NDVI area median per clear pass; the 30-day change is the latest pass against the last pass at least 30 days before it.
- Why green-up: migratory grazers trade grass quantity for quality and move to newly greened grass (Boone, Thirgood & Hopcraft 2006; Hopcraft et al. 2014). No collar or count is read here.

### Flood brief: Joshimath slopes, Uttarakhand, 2026-10-30 (SENTINEL-1)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Has fresh bare ground opened on the slopes around Joshimath?

#### Answer

Landslide rain watch elevated; 90-day rain near normal (z +0.1); next 7 days 45 mm, wetter than 94% of these weeks; no new fresh bare ground on the slopes (landslide scars) in the last 60 days (to 2026-10-22); window total 17 cells, most in 2024-02.

| month the loss was seen | cells | km² |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-02 | 10 | 1.60 |
| 2024-03 | 1 | 0.16 |
| 2024-12 | 4 | 0.64 |
| 2025-03 | 2 | 0.32 |

The largest drops:

- cell r09c11: NDVI 0.71 on 2024-02-15, 0.12 on 2024-02-25, and still down after
- cell r00c03: NDVI 0.51 on 2024-11-26, -0.03 on 2024-12-31, and still down after
- cell r00c05: NDVI 0.47 on 2024-11-26, -0.04 on 2024-12-31, and still down after
- cell r00c04: NDVI 0.48 on 2024-11-26, -0.03 on 2024-12-31, and still down after
- cell r09c10: NDVI 0.67 on 2024-02-15, 0.16 on 2024-02-25, and still down after
- cell r05c00: NDVI 0.86 on 2024-02-15, 0.37 on 2024-02-25, and still down after
- cell r07c01: NDVI 0.77 on 2024-02-15, 0.28 on 2024-02-25, and still down after
- cell r06c01: NDVI 0.79 on 2024-02-15, 0.36 on 2024-02-25, and still down after

#### Rain behind and ahead

- Last 7 days (to 2026-10-29): **1 mm**, at percentile 20 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Last 30 days (to 2026-10-29): **66 mm**, at percentile 57 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Last 90 days (to 2026-10-29): **855 mm**, at percentile 53 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- Next 3 days (forecast from 2026-10-30): **45 mm**, at percentile 98 of these weeks since 1996 (extremely wet).
- Next 7 days (forecast from 2026-10-30): **45 mm**, at percentile 94 of these weeks since 1996 (very wet).
- Next 14 days (forecast from 2026-10-30): **45 mm**, at percentile 83 of these weeks since 1996 (near normal).
- **Landslide rain watch: elevated.** Because: forecast 3-day 45 mm (percentile 98). A watch is raised when a 3- or 7-day total, past or forecast, is above the global minimum for triggering shallow landslides (Guzzetti et al. 2008: 24 mm over 3 days, 39 mm over 7) and among the wettest 5% (elevated) or 1% (high) of those weeks since the climatology began. It reads rain only, not soil, slope or what has already moved.
- The days ahead are a weather model's forecast, issued when this record was signed; past days are reanalysis (ERA5) or that model's own analysis, not a rain gauge.
- The ranking compares totals with ERA5's at the same place. The forecast model and ERA5 are different models on different grids, and ERA5 is known to under-read short convective bursts, so a forecast total ranks high a little more easily than an observed one would.
- Signed rain series: `emem:fact:defi.zb55b.zihO.gAgA:d54zaygop6iwyehwhifclbwyufhmqzlwnftpitbxls7hsoogra7a`.

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells (0.160 km² each) over a box 4.8 km a side. A cell counts when a clear pass reads at least 0.25 below the previous one in NDVI, the previous one was at least 0.4, and the next two passes stay at least half that drop below it: a missed cloud lasts one pass, a scar stays. Seasonal browning is gradual and does not count; harvest does, so this desk watches forests and slopes, not cropland.
- What it cannot tell apart from the series alone: a landslide from a burn or a clearing. The place says which it watches for; read a count as "vegetation lost", then look.
- Box: latitude 30.5334 to 30.5766, longitude 79.5400 to 79.5900.

#### Conclusions, as signed inferences

- `vegetation_loss@1`: `emem:fact:defi.zb55b.zihO.gAgA:yfleb6p7swam536ybsmol6qwfdfmllwc5qvrpebr23sbb64ej3ha`

- Signed series: `emem:fact:defi.zb55b.zihO.gAgA:d54zaygop6iwyehwhifclbwyufhmqzlwnftpitbxls7hsoogra7a`.

### Kailash-region brief: Mount Kailash summit block, 2026-10-30 (KAILASH)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

How much of the Kailash summit block is under snow, against the same weeks of earlier years?

#### Answer

**81%** of the area read snow or ice on the pass of 2026-10-27: about 13.0 km² of the 16.0 km² studied, from 159113 pixels clear of cloud.
In the same weeks of earlier years (29 passes within 15 days of the day of year) the median was 37%: +44 points this year.
Over the window the share ran from 14% on 2025-07-06 to 100% on 2022-03-07, across 261 usable passes.

| pass | snow or ice | cells seen |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-25 | 57% | 159095 |
| 2026-06-19 | 60% | 153011 |
| 2026-06-21 | 47% | 115842 |
| 2026-09-19 | 51% | 159200 |
| 2026-09-24 | 46% | 159196 |
| 2026-09-29 | 96% | 159201 |
| 2026-10-04 | 92% | 159201 |
| 2026-10-16 | 86% | 159201 |
| 2026-10-17 | 85% | 159081 |
| 2026-10-19 | 84% | 159201 |
| 2026-10-22 | 82% | 158939 |
| 2026-10-27 | 81% | 159113 |

#### Outlook: snow or ice

- **81% on 2026-11-10** (80% band 63% to 99%), 14 days ahead, by the persistence method. Over 228 past cases in this series it erred by 11 points on average; persistence (today's value) by 11 points, the season alone by 21 points; it does not beat both, so read it as no better than they are.
- **81% on 2026-11-24** (80% band 50% to 100%), 28 days ahead, by the persistence method. Over 216 past cases in this series it erred by 17 points on average; persistence (today's value) by 17 points, the season alone by 20 points; it does not beat both, so read it as no better than they are.

#### Method

- Test per cell: of the pixels clear of cloud, the share Sen2Cor's scene classification calls snow or ice (SCL class 11), from two signed series over the same box: one with the default cloud mask, one keeping class 11 only.
- Area: a box 4.0 km a side; a pass counts when at least 60% of the box is clear of cloud.
- Box: latitude 31.0498 to 31.0858, longitude 81.2909 to 81.3329.

### Proposed registry entry: seasonal_loss[ndvi,drop=0.30,from=0.3,post=45d] (proposed, awaiting replication)

Found by search, not written by hand: the methods lab searched 32 variants of a rule family and scored its picks on sites they never saw. Out of sample the search beat the registry's `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` on the pre-registered rule, by MCC. #### Clearings found, by size

Hansen draws each clearing as 8-connected 30 m pixels that lost cover in the scored years (forest in 2000). A method finds one when any cell it touches was flagged, so a method that flags much of the forest finds clearings by chance: beside each count, in brackets, is what its own flag rate on stable forest would find at random. #### Reading it

- A method beats the registry baseline only when the whole 95% interval of its MCC minus the baseline's lies above zero; a better point score inside an interval that crosses zero is a tie.
- The reference is Landsat-based and annual, so a loss Sentinel-2 sees in January can belong to the previous year in it; cells that lost cover in 2023 are left out of the stable set for that reason.
- Cells are 400 m: a clearing under 5% of a cell is left out rather than scored either way.

#### False alarms: stated in advance, then observed

Each of these methods calibrates its alarm on the cell's own remembered noise and states its chance of flagging a stable cell over the window before any data is read. Observed on this experiment's stable cells, with a Wilson 95% interval:

- `lab:memory_mv_optical@2`: stated 5%, observed 4 of 639 (0.6%, 0.2% to 1.6%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion@2`: stated 5%, observed 13 of 639 (2.0%, 1.2% to 3.4%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_mv_fusion_emp@3`: stated 5%, observed 10 of 639 (1.6%, 0.9% to 2.9%): calibrated.
- `lab:memory_hls_emp@4`: stated 5%, observed 8 of 639 (1.3%, 0.6% to 2.5%): calibrated.

#### The search, scored on sites it never saw

32 variants of the seasonal rule were searched. For each site the variant with the best MCC on the other sites was applied to it; over all sites those out-of-sample picks score **MCC 0.402**, and their MCC minus the baseline's has a 95% interval of +0.165 to +0.320: the searched rule beats the registry baseline.

Picks per held-out site:

- Sao Felix do Xingu, Para: `lab:seasonal_loss[nbr,drop=0.15,from=0.3,post=45d]`
- Boca do Acre, Amazonas: `lab:seasonal_loss[ndvi,drop=0.30,from=0.3,post=45d]`

### Agriculture-india brief: Lahaul valley farm, 2026-10-30 (AGENT A)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Where is this high valley's one short season, against last year?

#### Answer

79 cells are in the season under way, which peaked around **2026-07-27**. It has greened down (NDVI fell through half its amplitude and stayed down) in **45 of 79** by the pass of 2026-10-30; 3 are at their peak on the last pass. Green-down dates the end of the crop's growth: harvest follows it by days to weeks, so read this as how far the season has run, not as the harvest itself.
Like for like, over the 53 cells that also had a season peaking at the same time a year earlier: 42 have greened down by 2026-10-30, and 33 had by 2025-10-30.
A new season is greening (its season ended, or none was under way, and it has climbed at least 0.15 above its lowest point since) in 3 of 100 cells; a year earlier, 6.

**Yield outlook (season vigour).** The green each cell has built so far this season (NDVI accumulated above its starting level, from its lowest point of the last 150 days to 2026-10-30) against the same calendar span a year earlier: the median cell is at **1.14x** last year's, and 4 of 5 are above it. Season-integrated NDVI tracks yield in many crops, so this says which way the harvest leans against last year; it is not tonnes per hectare. 17 cells were left out because the two seasons were not seen on a similar number of clear passes.

no mapped field polygons here (0 found), so a grid of 10 x 10 cells of about 140 m over 1.4 km stands in for fields: a cell can hold more than one field, so read its season as the dominant one. Their median seasonal NDVI swing is 0.48.

### Coast brief: Rosetta promontory, Nile delta, 2026-10-31 (COAST)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Is the Rosetta promontory still retreating, and how fast?

#### Answer

No trend that the scatter allows (-0.4 m a year, 95% interval -10.6 to +9.6). Over 3.0 years of clear passes the sea reached a median of 1307 m into this 2.4 km box from its west edge; the Theil-Sen trend is -0.4 m a year of shore position (positive seaward), against a typical pass-to-pass scatter of 19 m.

| pass | sea width (m) | transects |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-25 | 1276 | 11 |
| 2026-05-10 | 1277 | 12 |
| 2026-06-04 | 1275 | 12 |
| 2026-06-24 | 1217 | 12 |
| 2026-07-04 | 1313 | 12 |
| 2026-07-14 | 1298 | 12 |
| 2026-07-24 | 1323 | 12 |
| 2026-08-08 | 1308 | 12 |
| 2026-08-18 | 1306 | 12 |
| 2026-09-07 | 1343 | 11 |
| 2026-10-09 | 1282 | 9 |
| 2026-10-29 | 1327 | 12 |

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells of 200 m over a box 2.4 km a side. Each cell's water fraction comes from its NDWI 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles (the share of pixels above 0.00, McFeeters 1996), so a shoreline moving a tenth of a cell shows. Each row running out to sea is a transect: the water counted from the sea edge until the first mostly-dry cell, so lagoons and flooded fields behind the beach do not count.
- Not corrected for tide, wave run-up or the season's sand cycle: that is most of the scatter, and the robust trend over many passes is what averages it out. A trend whose 95% interval (Sen 1968, from the ranks of the pairwise slopes) includes zero is reported as no trend.
- Box: latitude 31.4492 to 31.4708, longitude 30.3474 to 30.3726.

#### Conclusions, as signed inferences

- `shoreline_trend@1`: `emem:fact:defi.zb565.zf1e5.qozU:tzzqreuownnnnnd7rvnmajje5y2fbtptcbh2o42ogakginjtl66q`

- Why this place is on the desk: since the Aswan dam cut the Nile's sediment, the delta's tip has retreated by kilometres.

### Forest-and-fire brief: Jasper, Alberta, 2026-10-31 (FOREST)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

How much forest has burned here, and is it greening back?

#### Answer

No new burn scars in the last 60 days (to 2026-10-30); window total 143 cells, most in 2024-04.

| month the loss was seen | cells | km² |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-02 | 1 | 0.16 |
| 2024-04 | 132 | 21.12 |
| 2024-05 | 1 | 0.16 |
| 2024-08 | 8 | 1.28 |
| 2026-04 | 1 | 0.16 |

The largest drops:

- cell r00c01: NBR 0.63 on 2024-07-20, -0.43 on 2024-08-14, and still down after
- cell r00c02: NBR 0.61 on 2024-07-20, -0.41 on 2024-08-14, and still down after
- cell r01c01: NBR 0.52 on 2024-07-20, -0.42 on 2024-08-14, and still down after
- cell r02c08: NBR 0.53 on 2024-07-20, -0.40 on 2024-08-01, and still down after
- cell r01c03: NBR 0.52 on 2024-07-20, -0.41 on 2024-08-14, and still down after
- cell r08c06: NBR 0.76 on 2024-03-07, -0.15 on 2024-04-01, and still down after
- cell r07c06: NBR 0.75 on 2024-03-07, -0.13 on 2024-04-01, and still down after
- cell r02c02: NBR 0.44 on 2024-07-20, -0.42 on 2024-08-14, and still down after

#### Signed alerts from the method the evidence supports

Method `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1`, chosen for a fire watch from the methods lab's catalogue (status replicated, forest-dependent; pooled MCC difference from the registry rule +0.109, +0.031 to +0.188). 1 cells flagged with a loss seen in the last 180 days, 1 of them new or changed since the last brief, each a signed `canopy_alert@1` fact whose parents are the series below and the cell's previous alert.
- cell r09c09: loss seen 2026-08-14, `emem:fact:defi.zb659.vUge.binu:zjqalzhztqqnwufwj56bmcg7y6whrbas5xbrs35o3czppc56usqa`

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells (0.160 km² each) over a box 4.8 km a side. A cell counts when a clear pass reads at least 0.27 below the previous one in NBR, the previous one was at least 0.3, and the next two passes stay at least half that drop below it: a missed cloud lasts one pass, a scar stays. Seasonal browning is gradual and does not count; harvest does, so this desk watches forests and slopes, not cropland. For fire the index is NBR and the drop is dNBR 0.27, moderate severity in Key & Benson (2006).
- What it cannot tell apart from the series alone: a landslide from a burn or a clearing. The place says which it watches for; read a count as "vegetation lost", then look.
- Box: latitude 52.8484 to 52.8916, longitude -118.1157 to -118.0443.

#### Conclusions, as signed inferences

- `vegetation_loss@1`: `emem:fact:defi.zb659.vUge.binu:2hse6jxkuuve7rnkd2gyuip3emtbxjoobdlsariyeijtdjwhzctq`

### Kailash-region brief: Manasarovar north shore, 2026-10-31 (KAILASH)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Is Manasarovar's north shore advancing or retreating, and how fast?

#### Answer

No trend that the scatter allows (+3.0 m a year, 95% interval -4.8 to +7.2). Over 4.4 years of clear passes the sea reached a median of 1349 m into this 2.4 km box from its south edge; the Theil-Sen trend is +3.0 m a year of shore position (positive seaward), against a typical pass-to-pass scatter of 17 m.

| pass | sea width (m) | transects |
|---|---|---|

| 2025-10-22 | 1347 | 12 |
| 2025-10-24 | 1341 | 12 |
| 2026-06-11 | 1298 | 9 |

| 2026-10-02 | 2333 | 10 |
| 2026-10-27 | 1383 | 12 |

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells of 200 m over a box 2.4 km a side. Each cell's water fraction comes from its NDSI 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles (the share of pixels above -0.10, measured at this water against the land beside it), so a shoreline moving a tenth of a cell shows. Each row running out to sea is a transect: the water counted from the sea edge until the first mostly-dry cell, so lagoons and flooded fields behind the beach do not count.
- Not corrected for tide, wave run-up or the season's sand cycle: that is most of the scatter, and the robust trend over many passes is what averages it out. A trend whose 95% interval (Sen 1968, from the ranks of the pairwise slopes) includes zero is reported as no trend.
- Box: latitude 30.7692 to 30.7908, longitude 81.4655 to 81.4905.

### Coast brief: Marina Beach, Chennai, 2026-11-01 (COAST)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Is Marina Beach growing or shrinking, and how fast?

#### Answer

No trend that the scatter allows (+2.1 m a year, 95% interval -0.8 to +4.8). Over 2.9 years of clear passes the sea reached a median of 1169 m into this 2.4 km box from its east edge; the Theil-Sen trend is +2.1 m a year of shore position (positive seaward), against a typical pass-to-pass scatter of 10 m.

| pass | sea width (m) | transects |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-09 | 1168 | 12 |
| 2026-04-19 | 1174 | 12 |
| 2026-04-26 | 1154 | 12 |
| 2026-05-16 | 1175 | 12 |

| 2026-09-26 | 1179 | 12 |
| 2026-10-06 | 1183 | 9 |

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells of 200 m over a box 2.4 km a side. Each cell's water fraction comes from its NDWI 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles (the share of pixels above 0.00, McFeeters 1996), so a shoreline moving a tenth of a cell shows. Each row running out to sea is a transect: the water counted from the sea edge until the first mostly-dry cell, so lagoons and flooded fields behind the beach do not count.
- Not corrected for tide, wave run-up or the season's sand cycle: that is most of the scatter, and the robust trend over many passes is what averages it out. A trend whose 95% interval (Sen 1968, from the ranks of the pairwise slopes) includes zero is reported as no trend.
- Box: latitude 13.0392 to 13.0608, longitude 80.2729 to 80.2951.

### Agriculture-global brief: Mekong delta rice near Can Tho, 2026-11-01 (AGENT B)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

How many rice crops do these fields grow in a year, and where is the current one?

#### Answer

33 fields are in the season under way, which peaked around **2026-08-27**. It has greened down (NDVI fell through half its amplitude and stayed down) in **27 of 33** by the pass of 2026-10-31; 4 are at their peak on the last pass. Green-down dates the end of the crop's growth: harvest follows it by days to weeks, so read this as how far the season has run, not as the harvest itself.
Like for like, over the 17 fields that also had a season peaking at the same time a year earlier: 17 have greened down by 2026-10-31, and 12 had by 2025-10-31.
A new season is greening (its season ended, or none was under way, and it has climbed at least 0.15 above its lowest point since) in 4 of 58 fields; a year earlier, 0.

#### What was studied

58 real field polygons within about 1.4 km (the largest, at least 1,000 m² each; Fields of The World, CC-BY-4.0). Their median seasonal NDVI swing is 0.81.

#### Crop seasons in the window, grouped by when they peaked

Groups are the dates most fields peak near (the modes of the peak dates); each counts a field once per season. The crops are not named: the seasons come out of the data. Method: per field: NDVI area median per pass (field_series fields mode); a pass reading more than 0.1 below both neighbours is left out (cloud the mask missed); 3-pass running median; peaks closer than 60 days are one season; per-season amplitude threshold 0.5 (TIMESAT; White et al. 1997), each side of a season judged on its own amplitude (at least 0.15); an end counts only if the curve stays under the line for 20 days.

| 2025-11-25 | 7 | 2025-10-13 (2025-09-13..2025-10-23) | 2025-12-02 (2025-12-02..2025-12-30) | 3 |
| 2026-02-03 | 49 | 2025-12-20 (2025-12-15..2025-12-20) | 2026-03-02 (2026-02-28..2026-03-07) | 47 |

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells (0.160 km² each) over a box 4.8 km a side. ### Kailash-region brief: Rakshastal east shore, 2026-11-01 (KAILASH)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Is Rakshastal's east shore advancing or retreating, and how fast?

#### Answer

The shore is advancing seaward 15.0 m a year (95% interval 8.5 to 24.6; beach expansion). Over 4.4 years of clear passes the sea reached a median of 1047 m into this 2.4 km box from its west edge; the Theil-Sen trend is +15.0 m a year of shore position (positive seaward), against a typical pass-to-pass scatter of 43 m.

| pass | sea width (m) | transects |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-10-09 | 996 | 9 |
| 2025-10-12 | 993 | 9 |
| 2025-10-17 | 992 | 9 |
| 2025-10-21 | 998 | 9 |
| 2025-10-24 | 1087 | 12 |
| 2026-06-06 | 1002 | 9 |
| 2026-08-28 | 995 | 9 |
| 2026-08-30 | 1120 | 12 |
| 2026-10-14 | 988 | 9 |
| 2026-10-16 | 1000 | 9 |
| 2026-10-22 | 1189 | 9 |
| 2026-10-27 | 990 | 9 |

#### Method

- A grid of 12 x 12 cells of 200 m over a box 2.4 km a side. Each cell's water fraction comes from its NDSI 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles (the share of pixels above -0.10, measured at this water against the land beside it), so a shoreline moving a tenth of a cell shows. Each row running out to sea is a transect: the water counted from the sea edge until the first mostly-dry cell, so lagoons and flooded fields behind the beach do not count.
- Not corrected for tide, wave run-up or the season's sand cycle: that is most of the scatter, and the robust trend over many passes is what averages it out. A trend whose 95% interval (Sen 1968, from the ranks of the pairwise slopes) includes zero is reported as no trend.
- Box: latitude 30.6382 to 30.6598, longitude 81.3145 to 81.3395.

Over 2.9 years of clear passes the sea reached a median of 1324 m into this 2.4 km box from its east edge; the Theil-Sen trend is +6.6 m a year of shore position (positive seaward), against a typical pass-to-pass scatter of 28 m.

### Kailash-region brief: Lake Manasarovar, central basin, 2026-11-01 (KAILASH)

Written by an automated research agent from signed emem responses and test runs. Every number below comes from the token or record beside it; the wording is fixed text, not a model's summary.


#### The question

Is Lake Manasarovar frozen, and when did its ice form and go out last winter?

#### Answer

**100%** of the area read open water on the pass of 2026-10-27: about 92.2 km² of the 92.2 km² studied, from 100 of 100 cells the pass saw clearly.
In the same weeks of earlier years (27 passes within 15 days of the day of year) the median was 100%: about the same.
Over the window the share ran from 0% on 2021-12-09 to 100% on 2021-11-04, across 378 usable passes.

Ice periods in the window (ice months only, at least half the lake off open water, two passes or more):

- 2022-01-28 to 2022-04-11, 19 passes
- 2023-01-26 to 2023-04-18, 24 passes
- 2024-02-10 to 2024-02-15, 3 passes
- 2024-03-03 to 2024-04-02, 9 passes
- 2025-02-09 to 2025-03-28, 13 passes
- 2026-01-30 to 2026-02-04, 2 passes
- 2026-02-11 to 2026-03-16, 12 passes

| pass | open water | cells seen |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-12 | 100% | 100 |
| 2026-09-17 | 100% | 87 |
| 2026-09-19 | 100% | 72 |
| 2026-09-24 | 100% | 100 |
| 2026-09-29 | 76% | 99 |
| 2026-10-02 | 100% | 100 |
| 2026-10-07 | 100% | 100 |
| 2026-10-16 | 100% | 100 |
| 2026-10-17 | 100% | 100 |
| 2026-10-19 | 97% | 100 |
| 2026-10-22 | 100% | 100 |
| 2026-10-27 | 100% | 100 |

#### Outlook: open water

- **100% on 2026-11-10** (80% band 94% to 100%), 14 days ahead, by the anomaly method. Over 286 past cases in this series it erred by 11 points on average; persistence (today's value) by 14 points, the season alone by 11 points.
- **100% on 2026-11-24** (80% band 95% to 100%), 28 days ahead, by the anomaly method. Over 283 past cases in this series it erred by 11 points on average; persistence (today's value) by 23 points, the season alone by 10 points; it does not beat both, so read it as no better than they are.

#### Method

- Test per cell: NDMI below 0.50 on the cell median: over three years of both lakes, open water read up to 0.38 and ice from 0.62, because ice and snow are bright in near infrared and dark in shortwave infrared, while sun glint lifts both; thin wet ice at break-up reads as water. Passes the scene check calls suspect are kept: freezing and opening are sudden.

#### The question

Is Lake Rakshastal frozen, and when did its ice form and go out last winter?

#### Answer

**100%** of the area read open water on the pass of 2026-10-24: about 49.0 km² of the 49.0 km² studied, from 54 of 81 cells the pass saw clearly.
In the same weeks of earlier years (28 passes within 15 days of the day of year) the median was 100%: about the same.
Over the window the share ran from 0% on 2021-12-09 to 100% on 2021-11-07, across 373 usable passes.

#### Outlook: open water

- **100% on 2026-11-07** (80% band 71% to 100%), 14 days ahead, by the anomaly method. Over 283 past cases in this series it erred by 16 points on average; persistence (today's value) by 18 points, the season alone by 15 points; it does not beat both, so read it as no better than they are.
- **100% on 2026-11-21** (80% band 79% to 100%), 28 days ahead, by the anomaly method. Over 282 past cases in this series it erred by 15 points on average; persistence (today's value) by 24 points, the season alone by 14 points; it does not beat both, so read it as no better than they are.

#### Method

- Test per cell: NDMI below 0.50 on the cell median: over three years of both lakes, open water read up to 0.38 and ice from 0.62, because ice and snow are bright in near infrared and dark in shortwave infrared, while sun glint lifts both; thin wet ice at break-up reads as water. Passes the scene check calls suspect are kept: freezing and opening are sudden.
- Area: a grid of 9 x 9 cells, 0.60 km² each, over a box 7.0 km a side; a pass counts when it saw at least 60% of the cells through the cloud mask, and passes emem marks suspect are left out.
- Box: latitude 30.6236 to 30.6864, longitude 81.2135 to 81.2865.
